## [2026-06-06T21:30:55Z] assistant_thought (afterAgentThought)

The fix is to add `set-root: ok` to `main.scene.dry`. This makes the root scene ID become 'main' when the player enters main gameplay. Cards will then return to main instead of root.

Two more files need fixing. `cancel_advisor_action.scene.dry` should use `go-to: main` instead of `go-to: root`. `shuffle_cabinet.scene.dry` should use `- @return: No, there is no need.` instead of `- @root`.

During the new game bootstrap, rootSceneId remains 'root' until the player reaches main. Leaf subscenes triggered before main is reached would still return to root. This is unlikely during the organize phase.

rootSceneId persists in save state, so existing saves will correct themselves on the next visit to main. Whether post_event should also set-root is still being considered.

Leaf subscenes inside post_event flows would still return to rootSceneId. Events that fire after month advancement and before the first main visit would hit root instead of main. The default Continue behavior targets rootSceneId, so setting root only on main may not fully resolve the issue.

The player must reach main before drawing cards, so rootSceneId should already be 'main' during gameplay. Event scenes during post_event may still need their own @return or set-root.

## [2026-06-06T21:31:06Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Found two related problems and fixed all three touch points.

**Root cause (most cards):** When a card subscene has no choices left, Dendry shows a default “Continue…” button that goes to `rootSceneId`. That defaults to the `root` scene (start menu / setup), not `main`. Cards like contracting, community outreach, etc. hit this on their leaf subscenes.

**Explicit wrong targets:**
- `shuffle_cabinet` — “No, there is no need.” used `@root`
- `cancel_advisor_action` — had `go-to: root`

**Fixes:**

1. **`main.scene.dry`** — added `set-root: ok` so once you reach the main hand, “Continue…” on card subscenes returns to `main` instead of the start menu.

2. **`cancel_advisor_action.scene.dry`** — changed `go-to: root` → `go-to: main`.

3. **`shuffle_cabinet.scene.dry`** — changed `@root` → `@return` for the decline option.

Build and lint both pass. After reloading, finishing a card action should return you to the main hand; shuffle cabinet decline and advisor cancel should as well. Existing saves will pick up the new `rootSceneId` the next time they visit `main`.

The safer fix is to check prevSceneId inside return.scene.dry: only restore the card if the previous scene was a card scene or its subscene. This prevents stale state from ever triggering a restoration.

This eliminates the need to clear lastPlayedCard entirely. I verified the flow: playing a card sets lastPlayedCard and the scene ID, and @return correctly routes back to the card root.

  "content": "title: Education and training\nnew-page: true\nis-card: true\ncard-image: img/asteroid.jpg\ntags: local_organizing, city_affairs\nview_if: organizing_unlock = 1\n\nThe education system has both greatly advanced and greatly regressed since the pre-spaceflight era.  On the positive side, ubiquitous open sourced computerized educational resources have made it trivial for parents to provide children with basic life skills. On the negative side, most children are not recieving formal schooling.  Unschooled children are often left unprepared to the workforce and ignorant of world affairs.  The problem is particularly severe among the non-human populations from the otherworld.\n\n-@too_broke: We dont have the resources right now\n-@vocational\n-@home_ec\n-@well_rounded\n- @return\n\n@vocational\ntitle: Focus on vocational training to reduce poverty\nchoose-if: 1\non-arrival: vocational_track += 1\n\nImproving vocational training helps workers get better jobs, in particular with the corporations.  School attendence has risen somewhat as students are attracted by the prospect of higher incomes.  The megacorps approve of this curriculum and agree to contract some of their internal training programs over to our education system which allows us to offset the costs of this expansion.\n\n@home_ec\ntitle: Expand teaching of home economics skills like nutrition, health, electronics and mechanics\n\nWe strive to give students the skills to be more self reliant, making their food nuYen go farther, preventing health complications and repairing their home goods instead of buying new ones.  The cooperatives approve of this curriculum and some of their home schooled students have started attending classes part time.\n\n\n@well_rounded\ntitle: Provide a well rounded education\n\nWe are laying the foundation for a true public education system.  This is an expensive choice but will improve education outcomes across the board in the long term. {
  "file_path": "/home/airy/mikasa/source/scenes/cards/local_organizing/community_outreach.scene.dry",
  "content": "title: Community Conflicts\nnew-page: true\nis-card: true\ncard-image: img/asteroid.jpg\ntags: local_organizing\n\n= Community Conflicts\n\n- @first_wave_community\n- @second_wave_community\n- @isolated_communities\n- @drones_community\n- @otherworlders_community\n- @return\n\n@first_wave_community\ntitle: Calm the first wave settlers\nsubtitle: Japanese, European, American\non-arrival: first_wave_dissent -= 10; first_wave_strength += 1;\n\nThe first settlers were Japanese, whose numbers were joined by European and American colonists.  They are some of the best established and most prosperous people of Mikasa but the rivalries created by the chaos on earth leads to resentments in space, both between each other and towards the more recent arrivals.\n\nBy mediating and addressing private disputes and small conflicts, we have reduced unrest in this community.\n\n\n@second_wave_community\ntitle: Stabilize second wave communities\nsubtitle: Bantu, Middle Eastern, Southeastern Asian\non-arrival: second_wave_prosperity += 1; second_wave_dissent -= 5;\n\nMikasa and the other transsolar waystations became refugee destinations as the conflicts on Earth and the Jovian Moons worsened.  Many of the refugees came from places that had no previous ties to Mikasa.  The corporations were eager to have them come to serve as cheap labor but unconcerned with sustainable living conditions.  Uprooted from their existing support networks they have struggled but over time new communities are emerging.\n\nAddressing shortfalls in Mikasa's infrastructure and making connections with local community leaders helps address the poor living conditions and conflicts among these groups.\n\n@isolated_communities\ntitle: Outreach to isolated communities\nsubtitle: Deepers and Tunnel Clans\non-arrival: isolated_dissent -= 5;\n\nThe deepers are a community that originally settled on a different site of the asteroid from the tether ground station.  They intensely resent their annexation and desire a return to autonomy.  The tunnel clans are communities that left the artificial gravity grid and hid themselves away deep in the embrace of the \"mother\".  Their technical savviness could be an asset if we could overcome their isolation but this will be difficult as they can take care of their own and have little need for us.\n\n@drones_community\ntitle: Make inroads among the corporate employees\nsubtitle: Hereditary worker caste\non-arrival: drones_dissent -= 5;\n\nMost corporate employees on Mikasa work for the Big Three, Community Soylent, Magrail Combine and Brazos Universal.  Corporate employeeship has become a hereditary caste that jealously guards their privledges and relative wealth over the underclass.\n\nAny efforts to reach out to this group will inevitably be called illegal labor organizing.  Still there are more daring employees who have learned to keep things off the bosses radar.\n\n\n@otherworlders_community\ntitle: Assimilate arrivals from the otherworld\nsubtitle: Ruukish (otherworld humans), Fae, Orcs\non-arrival: otherworld_assimilation += 1;\n\nAlthough small in number, the refugees from the mystic otherworld have extreme culture shock.  What's worse they have brought a bitter ethnic conflict with them, the Orci question.  The orcs are often conflated with the orci, magical immitations of life while the fae are accused of ensnaring others in their magics.  The otherworld humans who typically are at the bottom of the heirarchy in the otherworld resent both groups but have trouble adjusting to a technological existence when they rarely possess basic literacy.\n\nWe can help educate the otherworlders in our ways, hopefullly learning from the times humanity has put aside it's conflicts instead of allowing them to fester.  And in turn we might learn more of the magical arts of the otherworld.  Even if few of the refugees were trained in the magical arts, they have seen far more magic then the vast majority of people from this world.\n"
}

The links between Mikasa and the Otherworld are not the most accessible or best travelled in the solar system but the Otherworlder population is proportonally large compared to the small population of Mikasa.  The situation hasn't drawn much notice to date except for the thriving {!<span class=\"tooltip-text\" style=\"color:rgba(149, 139, 0, 1);\" title=\"An non human sentient race from the otherworld, commonly called 'Elves' due to the cultural legacy of 20th century author and Otherworld explorer J.R.R. There are a larger number of otherworld travellers and an increase in {!<span class=\"tooltip-text\" style=\"color:rgba(18, 44, 4, 1);\" title=\"A greyish-green skinned sentient race from the otherworld.  They are frequently refered to by the racial slur 'Orcs' due to their close association with the sorcerers of the otherworld and their Orci creations. Our magical sages tell us the influx is driven by the overall trend towards travel getting easier (the long term cycle of otherworld alignment) and towards a new wave of demonic tyranny in the otherworld.\n\n-@problem: Another crisis to deal with...\n-@opportunity: ...or another opportunity to sieze?\n- @return\n\n\n@problem\ntitle: When it rains it pours.\n# dendry: was `@nothing The …` on one line (malformed id — prose must follow @subscene header)\n\nThe {!<span class=\"tooltip-text\" style=\"color:rgba(18, 44, 4, 1);\" title=\"A greyish-green skinned sentient race from the otherworld. Unlike most of the other's they tend to be illiterate and completely unfamiliar with modern technology.  While it would be humane to help them, they aren't a priority\n\n@opportunity\ntitle: ...or another opportunity to sieze?\n# dendry: was `@opportunity The …` on one line (malformed id)\n\nThe solar system has shown little interest in the otherworld besides in the magical arts of it's people. {
  "file_path": "/home/airy/mikasa/source/scenes/cards/local_organizing/peer_media.scene.dry",
  "content": "title: Media ideology \nnew-page: true\nis-card: true\ncard-image: img/asteroid.jpg\ntags: local_organizing\n\nThere are few proper outlets on Mikasa, the corporations shut down any independent competition with their propoganda that is too successful.  A handful of small outlets get by under the radar of the megacorps but most independent journalists rely on annonymous online peer to peer networks to get their reporting out.  Since most members of this small community follow each other's stories, the zeitgeist of the underground media shifts from time to time.\n\nDepending on what topics the underground is most interested in, different groups might become politically active.  What topics is the underground covering?\n\n-@labor\n-@wealthy\n-@diplomatic\n- @return\n\n@labor\ntitle: Abusive working conditions and the need for worker protections\nsubtitle: Popular among the poor and pisses off nobody but the megacorps\non-arrival: anti_corp_media += 1\n\nPopulist rhetoric is an easy way to get people wanting change.  The Stakeholder revolt might have been crushed but plenty of people are stakeholders in everything but name.\n\n@wealthy\ntitle: stress the need for self sufficiency and protection of businesses\nsubtitle: High skilled workers and cooperatives would like this but the establishment tone would be offputting to workers\nview-if: self_sufficiency_media = 0\non-arrival: self_sufficiency_media += 1\n\nTerrestrials or Martians might be surprised that discussions on IP restrictions on agrinutritional growth mediums can draw an audience but the matter is literally a matter of life and death for many in the cooperatives.  The wealthy usually are hostile towards the cooperatives but the discussion creates some cross-class solidarity, at least among the non-shareholder wealthy.\n\n@diplomatic\ntitle: discussion of Mikasa's place in the solar system economy and negotiations with megacorps\nsubtitle: We might be able to negotiate with corps in good faith, but any economic compromise would undermine self sufficiency\non-arrival: kiss_ass_media += 1\n\nMost people aren't interested in solarpolitical theory crafting but the podcast crowd keeps talking about it.  It doesn't move the needle on public opinion but maybe some good ideas will emerge from it."
}

## [2026-06-06T21:32:56Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Two changes work together: **`@return` on card menus** and **hand restoration in `return.scene.dry`**.

### Why this was needed
Playing a card removes it from your hand (`playCard`). Most deck cards had no way to back out — only a default “Continue…” after committing to an action. Advisors already used `- @return`; regular cards did not.

### `return.scene.dry`
When you `@return` from a played card, it now puts that card back in the main hand (if there’s room), using the previous scene to find the card root. Pinned advisor cards are unchanged — they never leave the pinned row.

### Cards updated with `- @return`
Added on the **top-level menu** of every deck card:

- community_outreach, contracting, activist_training, coop_economy, education, magic, migrations, peer_media  
- militia_degrade, municipal_ai, security  

`shuffle_cabinet` already had `@return` (“No, there is no need.”).

**Contracting submenus** also got `@return` so you can back out mid-choice:

- `@big_3`, `@local_wealthy`, `@cooperatives`

### Intentional omission on leaf choices
Subscenes where an action already fires on entry (e.g. “Calm the first wave settlers”) still end with “Continue…” only — the effect is already applied, so putting the card back in hand wouldn’t make sense.

Rebuild is done; reload and you should see a return option on card menus that puts the card back in your hand if you haven’t taken an action yet.

t < targets.length; t++) {\n            var id = targets[t].id\n            blockDeltas[id] = (blockDeltas[id] || 0) + transfer\n        }\n    }\n\n    accumulateSelfFeedback(state, q, blockDeltas, igDeltas, mult) {\n        if (this.toScope === 'ig') {\n            var igKey = this.igProsperityKey(this.toTarget)\n            var igVal = q[igKey]\n            if (igVal == null) { igVal = igProsperityDefault(this.toTarget) }\n            var igTransfer = this.coefficient * this.basisAmount(igVal) * mult\n            if (igTransfer !== 0) {\n                igDeltas[igKey] = (igDeltas[igKey] || 0) + igTransfer\n            }\n            return\n        }\n\n        var targets = this.blocksMatching(state, this.toScope, this.toTarget)\n        for (var t = 0; Syncing after patronage choices won't happen immediately. Fair bid selections trigger sync right away. Patronage route picks only update the other count, so the unlock check will wait until the next card visit.

An edge case exists where selecting patronage after the threshold is met could leave the chain unlocked. The unlock state persists once achieved, so the patronage option remains hidden.

Recalculating the unlock threshold on every sync risks toggling the state. If fair equals seven and other equals five, the chain unlocks and then immediately relocks. Before unlocking, patronage selections cannot push the other count high enough to break the threshold.

The unlock threshold rises as the other count increases. This prevents the chain from flipping back off after unlocking. A user can reach the unlock point while other equals zero, then select a second fair contract to secure the state. Old patronage selections made before unlocking remain valid.

## [2026-06-06T21:39:22Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Updated. Technocratic mode (`contract_fair_chain_complete`) now triggers when:

**fair contract uses ≥ patronage picks (excluding outside corps) + 3**

Examples:
- 0 Big Three / wealthy / coop awards → forced honest bidding after **3** fair contracts  
- 4 patronage awards → after **7** fair contracts  
- 10 different patronage routes used once each → after **13** fair contracts  

Outside corporation contracts aren’t counted on either side. Once the threshold is hit, the patronage menus hide and only honest bidding remains.

I need to track total contract counts and outside contract shares. This will let me show the outside option when fewer than one-quarter of contracts go to outside corporations.

The total contract count equals outside awards plus fair bids plus patronage awards. Outside awards are tracked by `contract_outside`. This gives the exact denominator for the one-quarter threshold.

The outside option appears when the fair chain is incomplete, or when it is complete but outside awards remain below one-quarter of total contracts. Edge cases were checked: zero total awards correctly trigger the display, while exactly one-quarter hides it.

I will precompute a boolean quality that marks the outside option eligible whenever outside awards are strictly below one-quarter of total contracts. This lets the Dendry view-if expression check the threshold directly. The logic will live inside `syncContractFairChainComplete` and will treat zero total awards as the default case.

The exact eligibility formula is now defined: `outsideCount * 4 < totalAwards`, or true when total awards are below one. The Dendry condition will use `or` between incomplete fair chain and low outside share. Subtitles must attach to the root menu choices themselves, since fair bidding always remains visible. The scene structure places `@outside_corporations` and `@fair_bidding` as sibling branches.

The subtitle text will be embedded directly in the Dendry `subtitle:` line for the `@outside_corporations` subscene. It will use conditional formatting, showing the competitive-bid text only when the fair chain is complete and the outside share is below one-quarter.

The `@outside_corporations` subscene will carry its own conditional subtitle, showing the competitive bid text only when the fair chain is complete and the outside share is low. The `@fair_bidding` subscene will instead use a subtitle that changes based on whether the fair chain is complete and whether any fair bids have been recorded.

t < targets.length; t++) {\n            var id = targets[t].id\n            blockDeltas[id] = (blockDeltas[id] || 0) + transfer\n        }\n    }\n\n    accumulateSelfFeedback(state, q, blockDeltas, igDeltas, mult) {\n        if (this.toScope === 'ig') {\n            var igKey = this.igProsperityKey(this.toTarget)\n            var igVal = q[igKey]\n            if (igVal == null) { igVal = igProsperityDefault(this.toTarget) }\n            var igTransfer = this.coefficient * this.basisAmount(igVal) * mult\n            if (igTransfer !== 0) {\n                igDeltas[igKey] = (igDeltas[igKey] || 0) + igTransfer\n            }\n            return\n        }\n\n        var targets = this.blocksMatching(state, this.toScope, this.toTarget)\n        for (var t = 0; ## [2026-06-06T21:44:45Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

In technocratic mode (patronage menus hidden), **Outside corporation suppliers** can still show if outside awards are **under 25%** of all contract awards.

**Share calculation** (in `syncContractFairChainComplete`):
- Total = `contract_outside` + `fair_contract_uses` + patronage picks (Big Three / wealthy / coop, each counted once)
- Outside share below quarter when `contract_outside × 4 < total`

**When both technocratic mode and under-quarter apply**, the two options show with:
- Outside: *"An outside corporation is making a very competitive bid"*
- Honest bidding: *"But we have reasonable grounds to favor domestic contractors"*

Once outside hits 25% or more of awards, only honest bidding remains in technocratic mode. Picking outside re-syncs the share so the option can drop off after that award.

The script will either reuse helpers from the existing simulation module or require it directly. A `--show-decays` flag will expose the current affluence decay rates for sanity checking. The parameter vector will use ten integer asset batches across the specified blocks and edges.

The optimizer will extract non-zero intra-district mesh pairs and IG home links from the default configuration. During each iteration it will override the simulation’s Q matrix parameters—starting asset batches, intra-district mesh, and IG home district links—before running the six-month simulation.

The script will initialize the economic simulation first, then remove the default starter assets and re-add them with the custom batch counts. This avoids patching the runtime before initialization.

Realized that `seedStarterEconomicAssets` hardcodes its starter asset batch counts inside a closure, so overriding them through the Q object alone will not work. Need to find another way to inject custom batch counts into the simulation.

The optimizer will duplicate the seed logic directly inside the script instead of editing the library. After initialization it will clear existing starter assets and rebuild them with custom batch counts using Q.addAsset.

The script will iterate over the default asset batches, round each custom count, and call `Q.addAsset` to recreate starter assets with the desired batch sizes. For the link parameters, it will deep-clone the default intra-district mesh and IG home district links, then assign them to `Q.prosperityIntraDistrictMeshDefault` and `Q.prosperityIgHomeDistrictLinks`. The default link schema may be captured during a one-time initialization or hardcoded from the scene file.

The optimizer will use random search with shrinking steps or coordinate descent rather than Nelder-Mead. It starts from baseline parameters, perturbs one or more values each iteration, and accepts the change only if the loss improves. Asset counts will be rounded to integers, and coefficients will be clamped to valid ranges. Parameter bounds are being set from zero up to roughly double the default counts or up to fifty.

Mesh coefficients will be bounded between 0 and 0.02. The loss function weights each block’s prosperity error by its population, applies a configurable residual multiplier, and adds a linkage penalty.

The loss formula will scale the weighted squared error by the configured residual multiplier and add a penalty equal to the sum of absolute link coefficients multiplied by a linkage weight. The optimizer will capture each block’s initial prosperity immediately after applying the custom asset batches but before the six-month simulation begins, ensuring the comparison reflects the seeded state rather than the true baseline.

The loss function will evaluate only VoterBlock prosperity, excluding IG prosperity. The optimizer will be registered as an npm script named `optimize-prosperity`. The decay table will list each stratum ID, scope, target, coefficient, self-feedback, and the monthly effect at prosperity ten.

## [2026-06-06T21:54:41Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Created `scripts/optimize-prosperity-balance.js` and wired it as `npm run optimize-prosperity`.

### Script behavior

Each evaluation:
1. Bootstraps election + economic runtimes from `.dry` scenes (same as `simulate-prosperity-months.js`)
2. Seeds starter assets and applies linkage coefficients from the parameter vector
3. Snapshots population-weighted block prosperity **after** seeding, **before** simulation
4. Runs **6 months** of prosperity tick (asset prosperity → connection bleed → housing)
5. Computes loss:

```
loss = residualMult × Σ pop×(final−initial)² / Σ pop  +  linkWeight × Σ|linkage coeffs|
```

**Tuned parameters (68 total):**
- 11 starter asset batch counts (`STARTER_ECONOMIC_ASSET_BATCHES`)
- 57 non-zero linkage coefficients (intra-district mesh + IG→home-district strata links)

**Fixed (not tuned):** affluence self-decay rows, Docks trade spill, Pitts crime, housing flow.

**CLI:**
```bash
npm run optimize-prosperity -- --iterations 300 --residual-mult 50 --link-weight 1 --verbose
npm run optimize-prosperity -- --show-decays
npm run optimize-prosperity -- --json-out out/prosperity-optim-result.json
```

The negotiation event will end with either `go-to: post_event` or `@return` after finalization.

The scene title is "Ceasefire Negotiations". It runs once and starts a new page. On arrival it sets up leverage and initializes cable_neg flags. A prose intro describes the neutral broker role. The scene then presents a terms menu.

Current leverage and reprisal appear in prose with inserts. The demands menu shows only available options based on prerequisites and prior selections. Subscenes cover police jurisdiction, funding, corporate tax, civil rights, ceasefire trials, judge review, disbanding corporate police, and prior leverage demands. Finalize deal and walk away are the two exit paths. Every subscene returns to the terms menu.

Helper functions will live in the on-arrival setup block. Leverage gains five points per demand. A JavaScript vote function compares each corporation’s remaining leverage against its reprisal plus the demand cost to decide whether to approve it.

The total reprisal cost will be tallied per demand and checked at finalization. Each demand carries distinct reprisal deltas for different corporations. Police jurisdiction maps Docks, Railyard, and Vats to Magrail and Soylent; Limelight to Brazos, but only if all three districts are already taken.

District police choices carry distinct reprisal costs. Vats police anger Soylent by two points. Railyard police anger Magrail by two points. Docks police anger both by one point. Limelight police anger Brazos by three points. Limelight is only available after all three districts are taken. The scene will use separate choices per district rather than a single multi-select hub.

## [2026-06-06T22:31:37Z] assistant_thought (afterAgentThought)

The broken links stem from a pattern in @terms_menu: `= Courts & rights` cannot appear between choice groups.

The fix is to remove inline section headings and link directly to existing category subscenes. This simplifies the menu while keeping all options reachable.

Section headers can be placed as HTML before the checklist rather than inside it. Bold labels already provide enough clarity. The root scene's go-to may need a fully qualified ID.

The broken links trace back to a parse error in `cable_break_negotiations.scene.dry` at line 80. That scene cannot compile until the error is fixed. The heading on line 80 appears after the choice list, which is invalid. Removing or moving those section headings before the first choice will resolve the compilation failure and restore the links.

HTML prose cannot be inserted between choice lines within a single options block. Once the parser sees a choice line, it expects only more choices until the next subscene. All section headers must therefore be grouped into one continuous prose block before the checklist begins.

The cleanest fix is to delete the four section headings entirely. The choice labels are already descriptive enough to guide the user without extra headers.

## [2026-06-06T22:31:47Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

The broken links came from a **Dendry parse error** in `@terms_menu`, not from the tax options themselves.

The hub had section headings (`= Security & jurisdiction`, `= Courts & rights`, etc.) **between** groups of `- @` choices. Dendry requires all choices in one contiguous block — any prose or headings after the first choice makes the whole scene fail to compile. That meant `cable_break_negotiations` never made it into the build, so every link to it (terms menu, corporate tax, dev jump, cable break event) was dead.

**Fix:** Removed the interleaved section headings and flattened `@terms_menu` into a single choice list. Also changed inline `@police_funding` in disband prose to plain text so it doesn’t render as a broken link.

`npm run make-html` succeeds now, so all negotiation options should work again. If you want the section groupings back visually, we can do it with category sub-menus (e.g. `@terms_security` → police/tax/disband) without breaking the parser.

Adding a system to withdraw demands from the deal.

A shared JavaScript helper block in bootstrap would cover both adding and withdrawing demands. Refactoring existing add paths is avoided to keep the scope minimal.

A central `Q.cableNegWithdraw` function is cleaner than separate menu items. It will use exact reprisal deltas to prevent drift. Bootstrap helpers `cableNegBumpReprisal` and `cableNegUnbumpReprisal` are being added.

The unbump helper will floor reprisal at zero. To keep scope small, the subtract logic will be duplicated directly into each withdraw choice rather than refactoring all add paths. Withdrawals will cascade through dependencies: removing limelight clears related infrastructure demands, police pay clears corporate tax, trials clear judge review, and education enrollment clears education pay.

Withdrawing pay will cascade to clear corporate tax. Pay may be orphaned if it was the sole jurisdiction for transfers, so it will be offered as a separate withdrawal option. Vats, railyard, and docks cannot be withdrawn while limelight is active; an unavailable subtitle will prompt users to withdraw limelight first.

The withdraw demands menu will only appear when at least one demand is active. A long Dendry `or` chain will check every demand flag to drive the `view-if` condition. A computed flag was considered but rejected as overkill.

Each withdraw choice will use `choose-if` to appear only when its demand is active. Tiered demands such as police pay, corporate tax, disband, trials, judge review, and infrastructure cap will use `switch` blocks to subtract the correct reprisal amount based on their current value. The `withdraw_demands` block will be placed after `terms_menu` and before `@police_jurisdiction`.

Each withdraw action will trigger `Q.syncIgAttitudes()` to refresh influence states. The menu title will be "Remove a demand" with a subtitle explaining reprisal reduction. Dendry may not support `view-if` on individual choice lines, so `choose-if` will be used for conditional visibility instead.

The withdraw menu will fall back to prose if no demands are active, showing only the terms menu. The repository pattern places `choose-if` on the `@subscene` block itself. Whether Dendry supports `view-if` on the parent choice in `terms_menu` is still uncertain.

The `view-if` guard will be placed directly on the `@withdraw_demands` block itself, following the existing `prior_leverage_demands` pattern. The full list of withdraw options is now ordered by dependency: corporate tax, police pay, limelight, vats, railyard, docks, disband, civil rights, judge review, trials, infrastructure cap, education pay, and education enrollment.

Land tax is being added to the withdraw menu. Police pay withdrawals will roll back reprisal by the full tier amount and cascade to clear corporate tax inline. Trial withdrawals will also clear judge review if it is currently set.

Integer quality ranges are confirmed. The four corporation categories will map to cable_neg_stance_soylent, cable_neg_stance_magrail, and cable_neg_stance_brazos.

A sync function computes each corporation's leverage-reprisal margin. Leverage minus reprisal above three maps to category four. Two to three maps to category three. One maps to category two. Anything below maps to category one.

The sync function will run on arrival at the terms menu. The root scene may also need it, since the user wants the update on every return to the main menu.

The sync function will also run after the player withdraws demands, since they return to the terms menu from there. Adding a demand sends them to a parent sub-menu instead, but they still reach the terms menu eventually. The first visit to the terms menu will be covered by the on-arrival trigger. (Number(Q.magrail_leverage) || 0) > Q.cable_neg_leverage_boost\n        || (Number(Q.brazos_leverage) || 0) > Q.cable_neg_leverage_boost\n    ) ? 1 : 0\n\n    Q.cable_neg_police_vats = 0\n    Q.cable_neg_police_railyard = 0\n    Q.cable_neg_police_docks = 0\n    Q.cable_neg_police_limelight = 0\n    Q.cable_neg_police_pay = 0\n    Q.cable_neg_corp_tax = 0\n    Q.cable_neg_corp_tax_fund = = 0\n    Q.cable_neg_education_pay = 0\n    Q.cable_neg_land_tax = 0\n    Q.cable_neg_infra_cap = 0\n}\nfunction cableNegReprisalAdd(corp, delta) {\n    Q[corp + '_reprisal'] = (Number(Q[corp + '_reprisal']) || 0) + delta\n}\nfunction cableNegReprisalAddEach(delta) {\n    cableNegReprisalAdd('soylent', delta)\n    cableNegReprisalAdd('magrail', delta)\n    cableNegReprisalAdd('brazos', delta)\n}\nfunction cableNegReprisalSub(corp, delta) {\n    Q[corp + '_reprisal'] = Math.max(0, (Number(Q[corp + '_reprisal']) || 0) - delta)\n}\nfunction cableNegClearCorpTax() {\n    var t = CABLE_NEG_REPR_TAX_HALF_BELL_MAGRAIL)\n    } else if (t === 2) {\n        cableNegReprisalSub('soylent', CABLE_NEG_REPR_TAX_FULL_BELL_SOYLENT)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('magrail', CABLE_NEG_REPR_TAX_HALF_ALL_EACH)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('brazos', CABLE_NEG_REPR_TAX_HALF_ALL_EACH)\n    } else if (t === 4) {\n        cableNegReprisalSub('soylent', CABLE_NEG_REPR_TAX_FULL_ALL_SOYLENT)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('magrail', CABLE_NEG_REPR_TAX_FULL_ALL_MAGRAIL)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('brazos', CABLE_NEG_REPR_TAX_FULL_ALL_BRAZOS)\n    }\n    Q.cable_neg_corp_tax = 0\n    Q.cable_neg_corp_tax_fund = 0\n    Q.cable_neg_brazos_tax_exempt = 0\n}\nfunction cableNegClearPolicePay() {\n    var pay = Number(Q.cable_neg_police_pay) || 0\n    if (pay === 1) {\n        cableNegReprisalSub('soylent', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_2X_EACH)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('magrail', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_2X_EACH)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('brazos', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_2X_EACH)\n    } else if (pay === 2) {\n        cableNegReprisalSub('soylent', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_6X_EACH)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('magrail', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_6X_EACH)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('brazos', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_6X_EACH)\n    } else if (pay === 3) {\n        cableNegReprisalSub('soylent', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_6X_MATCH_EACH)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('magrail', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_6X_MATCH_EACH)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('brazos', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_6X_MATCH_EACH)\n    } else if (pay === 4) {\n        cableNegReprisalSub('soylent', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_10X_SOYLENT)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('magrail', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_10X_MAGRAIL)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('brazos', CABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_10X_BRAZOS)\n    }\n    Q.cable_neg_police_pay = 0\n    if ((Number(Q.cable_neg_corp_tax) || 0) > 0) { cableNegClearCorpTax() }\n}\nfunction cableNegClearJudgeReview() {\n    var j = Number(Q.cable_neg_judge_review) || 0\n    if (j === 2) {\n        cableNegReprisalSub('soylent', CABLE_NEG_REPR_JUDGE_2_EACH)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('magrail', CABLE_NEG_REPR_JUDGE_2_EACH)\n CABLE_NEG_REPR_JUDGE_4_EACH)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('brazos', CABLE_NEG_REPR_JUDGE_4_EACH)\n    }\n    Q.cable_neg_judge_review = 0\n}\nfunction cableNegClearTrials() {\n    if ((Number(Q.cable_neg_judge_review) || 0) > 0) { cableNegClearJudgeReview() }\n    var t = Number(Q.cable_neg_trials) || 0\n    if (t === 1) {\n        cableNegReprisalSub('soylent', CABLE_NEG_REPR_TRIALS_CITY_SOYLENT)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('magrail', CABLE_NEG_REPR_TRIALS_CITY_MAGRAIL)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('brazos', CABLE_NEG_REPR_TRIALS_CITY_BRAZOS)\n    } else if (t === 2) {\n        cableNegReprisalSub('soylent', CABLE_NEG_REPR_TRIALS_MIXED_SOYLENT)\n        cableNegReprisalSub('magrail', CABLE_NEG_REPR_TRIALS_MIXED_MAGRAIL)\n    }\n    Q.cable_neg_trials = 0\n}\nfunction cableNegClearEducationEnroll() {\n    if (Q.cable_neg_education_pay === 1) {\n        cableNegReprisalAddEach(-CABLE_NEG_REPR_EDU_PAY_EACH)\n        Q.cable_neg_education_pay = 0\n    }\n    cableNegReprisalAddEach(-CABLE_NEG_REPR_EDU_ENROLL_EACH)\n    Q.cable_neg_education_enroll = 0\n}\nfunction cableNegSyncCorpStances() {\n    function stanceFor(corp) {\n        var margin = (Number(Q[corp + '_leverage']) || 0) - (Number(Q[corp + '_reprisal']) || 0)\n        var cat = 1\n        if (margin > 3) { cat = 4 }\n        else if (margin >= 2) { cat = 3 }\n        else if (margin >= 1) { cat = 2 }\n        Q['cable_neg_stance_' + corp] = cat\n    }\n    stanceFor('soylent')\n    stanceFor('magrail')\n    stanceFor('brazos')\n}\nif (typeof Q.syncIgAttitudes === 'function') { Q.syncIgAttitudes() }\n!}\n\nThe tether rupture left Community Soylent and Magrail Combine willing to talk — but only through us.  Brazos Zaibatsu sits at the table too, ostensibly as a neutral party but really as a party interested in screwing them both.  They need a neutral enforcer for the ceasefire; we need to decide what that costs them.\n\nLeverage (after crisis boost): Soylent [+ soylent_leverage +] / reprisal [+ soylent_reprisal +]; Magrail [+ magrail_leverage +] / [+ magrail_reprisal +]; Brazos [+ brazos_leverage +] / [+ brazos_reprisal +].\n\nAny package needs **two megacorps** to accept (leverage still above reprisal after our demands). ## [2026-06-06T22:53:28Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

All reprisal knobs now have inline comments naming the demand they belong to. There’s also a **rival schadenfreude** block (`CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_*`) for options where one megacorp enjoys a rival’s setback.

**Rival relief applies on:**
| Demand | Hurt | Relieved (enjoys rival’s pain) |
|--------|------|--------------------------------|
| Vats police | Soylent +2 | Magrail −1 |
| Railyard police | Magrail +2 | Soylent −1 |
| Docks police | Soylent +1, Magrail +1 | Brazos −1 |
| Limelight police | Brazos +3 | Soylent −1, Magrail −1 |
| Tax (half/full, belligerents only) | Soylent & Magrail | Brazos −1 |
| Mixed ceasefire trials | Soylent +1, Magrail +1 | Brazos −1 |

**Rules enforced in code:**
- Relief only runs when gross reprisal raised ≥ **2** on that pick
- Total relief is always **strictly less** than total raised (net reprisal still goes up)
- If knobs would break that, relief is auto-clamped so net gain is at least 1

Withdraw paths mirror the same math, so removing a demand restores rival relief too. Demands that hit everyone equally (payroll, civil rights, infra cap, tax-all-three, etc.) have no relief — edit only the `CABLE_NEG_REPR_*` lines for those.

## [2026-06-06T22:55:31Z] assistant_thought (afterAgentThought)

I'm examining the extract-scene-js script to simulate the on-arrival logic and identify why the leverage and reprisal values aren't updating.

Two likely causes emerged. Dendry may navigate away from a subscene before its on-arrival logic executes. Alternatively, `cableNegApplyVatsPolice()` is only defined during root scene on-arrival, so it is missing when the user moves between subscenes without restarting the root scene.

The function may be local to the root scene's on-arrival evaluation rather than global. That would cause a silent ReferenceError when the subscene tries to call it. I will inspect the compiled game.js to confirm how the on-arrival code is wrapped.

The demands checklist likely updates correctly because its flag assignments run before the apply function call. A total silent failure would break both the checklist and the display. The user probably means the "At the table" section isn't refreshing. This suggests the apply function itself is failing while the surrounding logic still succeeds.

I suspect the dynamic bracket notation in `cableNegReprisalAdd` is failing to write the quality values in Dendry. I will replace those assignments with direct property writes. I also plan to attach helper functions to the global `Q` object during root on-arrival so they remain accessible across subscene navigation.

The template likely reads a local JavaScript variable instead of the global Q quality. Since the contracting scene already writes to Q.soylent_reprisal successfully, the bracket notation is probably valid. The function scope issue remains the most likely culprit.

## [2026-06-06T22:56:19Z] assistant_thought (afterAgentThought)

A critical finding was identified in the JavaScript code.

The on-arrival function receives `state` and `state.qualities` as arguments. `Q` is therefore a local parameter, not a global variable. This explains why the leverage and reprisal values fail to update.

Helper functions declared inside on-arrival callbacks are scoped to that specific execution. When another on-arrival block tries to call them, a ReferenceError occurs. The runActions try/catch silently catches this error, so the update appears to succeed while actually doing nothing.

Subscene on-arrival blocks are separate compiled functions that cannot access root-scoped helpers. Constants like CABLE_NEG_REPR_VATS_SOYLENT are also lost outside the root block.

The fix is to register all helpers and constants directly on Q during root on-arrival. Subscene calls should then reference Q.cableNegApplyVatsPolice() instead of relying on closure scope.

The architecture is now clear. The issue appears to involve `Q`.

Subscenes reference bare `CABLE_NEG_*` constants instead of `Q.CABLE_NEG_*`. The API refreshes `Q` correctly, but the subscenes ignore those updates. Replacing bare references with `Q.CABLE_NEG_*` will fix the stale values.

The `ensureApi` helper functions close over local `CABLE_NEG_*` variables. They only capture the values from the first invocation. Later early returns refresh `Q` but do not update those closures. This creates a stale closure problem.

The stale closure is harmless for balance if values never changed. The real bug remains subscenes using bare `CABLE_NEG_*` constants. The helpers on `Q` should still work if `ensureApi` ran once from root.

Each subscene calls `Q.cableNegEnsureApi()` directly. The function is reassigned on every root on-arrival. First-time visitors therefore always hit the full setup path.

Subscenes do not execute root on-arrival. Root on-arrival always runs first and defines `ensureApi` on `Q`. Subscenes then call `Q.cableNegEnsureApi()` during their own on-arrival. This confirms the API setup happens before subscenes run.

The police helpers are confirmed on `Q`, so they work. Pay choices still use bare `CABLE_NEG_*` constants. I will patch the subscene references starting at line 566.

## [2026-06-06T22:58:35Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Not all variables — only the things that **subscene `on-arrival` blocks need to see** across Dendry’s scope boundary.

There are three buckets:

**1. Game state (unchanged — already on `Q`)**  
Things like `soylent_leverage`, `soylent_reprisal`, `cable_neg_police_vats`, `cable_neg_stance_soylent`. Those were always game qualities/stats on `Q`; that’s normal Dendry.

**2. Helper functions (new on `Q`)**  
`Q.cableNegApplyVatsPolice()`, `Q.cableNegReprisalAdd()`, etc. These used to be plain functions in the root `on-arrival`. Subscenes couldn’t call them, so they’re installed on `Q` once via `Q.cableNegEnsureApi()`.

**3. Balance constants (copied to `Q`)**  
The `CABLE_NEG_*` knobs at the top of the root block are still defined locally for easy editing. They’re also copied to `Q.CABLE_NEG_*` because a few subscenes (payroll, disband, withdraw handlers) reference those numbers directly instead of going through a helper.

So it’s not “everything lives on `Q`” — it’s “shared code and constants that subscenes need get attached to `Q` because that’s the one object every `on-arrival` block receives.”

That matches how this repo already handles cross-scene logic (`election_runtime`, `electorate_runtime`, etc.), just inlined in this scene instead of a separate silent setup scene.

If you’d rather not mirror constants onto `Q`, the cleaner shape would be:

- Keep the edit-at-the-top `CABLE_NEG_*` block in root only  
- Route **all** demand/withdraw logic through `Q.cableNegApply…()` / `Q.cableNegClear…()` helpers (no bare `Q.CABLE_NEG_*` in subscenes)  
- Optionally move the API into a hidden setup scene like the election runtime

That would drop the `Q.CABLE_NEG_*` duplication and leave `Q` with functions plus game state only. Want me to refactor it that way?

I checked the full chain — qdisplays, runtime sync, scene references, and the compiled build. **Everything is linked correctly.**

## General attitudes (Status screen)

**Qdisplay:** `source/qdisplays/attitude.qdisplay.dry` — codes 0–6 (Contempt → Furious)

**Runtime:** `attitude_runtime.scene.dry` maps leverage/reprisal → label → code:

| Code | Label | When |
|------|-------|------|
| 0 | Contempt | L + R < 3 |
| 1 | Wary | R ≥ L (moderate) |
| 2 | Transactional | L > R (moderate) |
| 3 | Tolerating | L > R, L + R > 18 |
| 4 | Hostile | R > L, L + R > 18 |
| 5 | Captive | L > R, L > 18 |
| 6 | Furious | R > L, R > 18 |

**Sync:** `Q.syncIgAttitudes()` writes `Q.attitude_{ig}` for all six IGs: `brazos`, `magrail`, `soylent`, `families`, `edges`, `sharks`.

**Display:** `status.scene.dry` uses the correct pattern:

```16:21:source/scenes/status.scene.dry
[+ attitude_brazos : attitude +]
[+ attitude_magrail : attitude +]
[+ attitude_soylent : attitude +]
[+ attitude_families : attitude +]
[+ attitude_edges : attitude +]
[+ attitude_sharks : attitude +]
```

Status calls `syncIgAttitudes()` on arrival, so labels stay current. Boot chain loads `attitude_runtime` via `setup_functions` before main.

**Build check:** compiled `core.js` has `"qdisplay":"attitude"` on those inserts, with all seven buckets matching the file.

---

## Negotiation stances (Cable break terms menu)

Separate system — finer-grained table talk, not the global attitude scale.

**Qdisplay:** `source/qdisplays/cable_neg_stance.qdisplay.dry` — codes 1–4 only

**Sync:** `Q.cableNegSyncCorpStances()` sets `Q.cable_neg_stance_{corp}` from leverage − reprisal margin:

| Code | Label | Margin |
|------|-------|--------|
| 1 | Considers this completely unacceptable | ≤ 0 |
| 2 | Barely willing to accept | 1 |
| 3 | Could maybe give up more | 2–3 |
| 4 | Willing to make concessions | > 3 |

**Display:** negotiations scene uses `[+ cable_neg_stance_soylent : cable_neg_stance +]` (and magrail/brazos). Compiled output confirms `"qdisplay":"cable_neg_stance"` on those inserts.

**Sync timing:** runs on `@terms_menu` arrival (and after demand changes via `syncIgAttitudes()` for the status-scale attitudes, not the neg stances).

---

## Sanity check at typical values

- New game corps (L=1, R=1): **Contempt** (0) — L+R < 3
- After +5 crisis boost (L=6, R=1): **Transactional** (2) on status; **Willing to make concessions** (4) at the neg table
- Adding reprisal (e.g. L=6, R=3): still Transactional on status; neg stance drops to **Could maybe give up more** (3)

Those are different scales on purpose — status is the long-term relationship chart; the neg menu is “how are they feeling about *this* package right now.”

---

## Minor notes (not broken, just worth knowing)

1. **`cable_neg_stance` has no bucket for 0** — but sync always writes 1–4 before the terms menu renders, so you shouldn't see a raw number.
2. **Dev jump** (`@dev_cable_neg`) skips `setup_functions`, so `syncIgAttitudes` is a guarded no-op there. Fine for testing negotiations (which use `cable_neg_stance`), but Status would show Contempt until a full boot loads `attitude_runtime`.

No wiring fixes needed — the qdisplay IDs, numeric codes, and sync functions all match.

## [2026-06-06T23:04:07Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

`Q.syncIgAttitudes()` is what updates the displayed attitudes. It reads each IG’s `{ig}_leverage` and `{ig}_reprisal`, runs them through `attitude()`, and writes the numeric code to `Q.attitude_{ig}` (what Status shows via the `attitude` qdisplay).

It is **defined once** in `attitude_runtime.scene.dry` during boot (`setup_functions` → `attitude_runtime` if missing). After that it only runs when something explicitly calls it — **not** every month.

## When it runs

| When | Where |
|------|--------|
| **Game boot** | `organize_phase_tick.scene.dry` setup (after runtimes load) — initial sync from starting leverage/reprisal |
| **Opening Status** | `status.scene.dry` root `on-arrival` |
| **Status → Politics tab** | `status.scene.dry` `@politics` `on-arrival` |
| **Contracting card** | After each big-3 contract choice (`@big_3_docks`, `@big_3_vats`, `@big_3_railyard`, `@big_3_limelight`) and `@coop_pitts` |
| **Cable negotiations** | Scene entry; every `@terms_menu` visit; every `@wd_*` withdraw; `@finalize_deal` |

For negotiations specifically: **adding** a demand doesn’t call `syncIgAttitudes` in that choice’s block, but those choices `go-to: terms_menu`, and **terms menu syncs on arrival**. So attitudes refresh when you land back on the table.

## When it does *not* run

- **`post_event` / monthly tick** — `monthly_tick_phase1()` syncs prosperity, budget, etc., but **not** attitudes.
- **Most other cards** — anything that doesn’t change leverage/reprisal, or that changes them without calling sync.
- **Some contracting paths** — e.g. `@coop_deeps` bumps prosperity but never calls sync (only matters if that choice changed leverage/reprisal; it doesn’t).
- **Dev jump to cable neg** — skips `setup_functions`, so `syncIgAttitudes` may not exist until a full boot (calls are guarded with `typeof … === 'function'`).

## Separate from negotiation stances

`Q.cableNegSyncCorpStances()` (the “At the table” labels) runs **only** on `@terms_menu` arrival. That’s independent of `syncIgAttitudes`.

---

**Bottom line:** `attitude_*` is a **derived display cache**, refreshed at boot, when you open Status, after contracting moves that change leverage/reprisal, and throughout cable negotiations (via terms menu / withdraw / finalize). It is **not** kept current automatically each month — if you want that, you’d add `syncIgAttitudes()` to `monthly_tick_phase1()`.

2000\nQ.affluent_money = 500\nQ.poor_money = 1000\nQ.coop_money = 1500\nQ.coop_capital = 10000\n\n/** Voter-block prosperity index (election_runtime MIKASA_BLOCK_PROSPERITY_BASE). */\nconst PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE = 6\n/** Corp/syndicate Q.prosperity_* at new game (root @start). */\nconst PROSPERITY_IG_START = {\n    Soylent: 10,\n    Magrail: 10,\n    Brazos: 10,\n    Families: 8,\n    Edges: 8,\n    Sharks: 8,\n}\n/** Display scale for stock / syndicate indices (prosperity 10 → baseline ticker). */\nconst PROSPERITY_IG_DISPLAY_BASE = 10\nconst PROSPERITY_CLAMP_MIN = 0\nconst PROSPERITY_CLAMP_MAX = 20\n/**\n * Monthly prosperity bleed between voter blocks (and corps/syndicates on Q).\n * Mirrors ElectorateModifier: catalog rows, optional stackId on Q for card-driven links.\n *\n * Positional:\n *   new ProsperityConnectionModifier(rowId, fromScope, fromTarget, toScope, toTarget, coefficient [, opts])\n * Object: { id, fromScope, fromTarget, toScope, toTarget, coefficient, basis?, self_feedback?, stackId?, activeIf? }\n *\n * basis: 'level' (default) | 'excess' (prosperity − block baseline, usually 6)\n * self_feedback: true → each destination uses its own prosperity as the source (stratum self-decay)\n * quality scope: fromTarget is a Q quality (e.g. trade_level); signal uses (value − 1) when basis is excess\n */\nclass ProsperityConnectionModifier {\n    constructor(rowId, fromScope, fromTarget, toScope, toTarget, coefficient, opts) {\n        if (rowId && typeof rowId === 'object') {\n            opts = rowId\n            rowId = opts.id\n            fromScope = opts.fromScope\n            fromTarget = opts.fromTarget\n            toScope = opts.toScope\n            toTarget = opts.toTarget\n            coefficient = opts.coefficient\n        } else if (typeof opts !== 'object' || opts === null) {\n            opts = {}\n        }\n        this.id = rowId\n        this.fromScope = fromScope\n        this.fromTarget = fromTarget || ''\n        this.toScope = toScope\n        this.toTarget = toTarget || ''\n        this.coefficient = coefficient || 0\n        this.basis = opts.basis || 'level'\n        this.self_feedback = !!(opts.self_feedback || opts.local)\n        this.stackId = opts.stackId || null\n        this.activeIf = opts.activeIf || function() { return true }\n    }\n\n    stacksFromQ(q) {\n        if (!this.stackId) { return 1 }\n        if (!q || q[this.stackId] == null) { return 0 }\n        var n = Number(q[this.stackId])\n        if (isNaN(n) || n <= 0) { return 0 }\n        return n\n    }\n\n    isActive(q) {\n        try {\n            return !!this.activeIf(q)\n        } catch (e) {\n            return false\n        }\n    }\n\n    basisAmount(value) {\n        var v = Number(value)\n        if (isNaN(v)) { v = defaultProsperityForConnection(this) }\n        if (this.basis === 'excess') {\n            if (this.fromScope === 'quality') {\n                return v - 1\n            }\n            return v - PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE\n        }\n        return v\n    }\n\n    igProsperityKey(igId) {\n        return 'prosperity_' + String(igId).toLowerCase()\n    }\n\n    blocksMatching(state, scope, target) {\n        if (!state || !state.blocks) { return [] }\n        if (scope === 'block') {\n            return state.blocks.filter(function(b) { return b.id === target })\n        }\n        if (scope === 'stratum') {\n            return state.blocks.filter(function(b) { return b.demographic.id === target })\n        }\n        if (scope === 'district') {\n            return state.blocks.filter(function(b) { return b.district.id === target })\n        }\n        return []\n    }\n\n    weightedBlockProsperity(blocks) {\n        var popSum = 0\n        var weighted = 0\n        for (var i = 0; i < blocks.length; i++) {\n            var b = blocks[i]\n            var pop = b.population\n            if (pop <= 0) { continue }\n            popSum += pop\n            weighted += pop * (b.prosperity ?? PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE)\n        }\n        return popSum > 0 ? weighted / popSum : PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE\n    }\n\n    readBroadcastSource(state, q) {\n        if (this.fromScope === 'quality') {\n            var raw = Number(q[this.fromTarget])\n            if (isNaN(raw)) { raw = 1 }\n            return this.basisAmount(raw)\n        }\n        if (this.fromScope === 'ig') {\n            var key = this.igProsperityKey(this.fromTarget)\n            var igVal = q[key]\n            if (igVal == null) { igVal = igProsperityDefault(this.fromTarget) }\n            return this.basisAmount(igVal)\n        }\n        var blocks = this.blocksMatching(state, this.fromScope, this.fromTarget)\n        return this.basisAmount(this.weightedBlockProsperity(blocks))\n    }\n\n    accumulate(state, q, blockDeltas, igDeltas) {\n        if (!this.isActive(q)) { return }\n        var mult = this.stacksFromQ(q)\n        if (mult <= 0) { return }\n\n        if (this.self_feedback) {\n            this.accumulateSelfFeedback(state, q, blockDeltas, igDeltas, mult)\n            return\n        }\n\n        var sourceSignal = this.readBroadcastSource(state, q)\n        var transfer = this.coefficient * sourceSignal * mult\n        if (transfer === 0) { return }\n\n        if (this.toScope === 'ig') {\n            var igKey = this.igProsperityKey(this.toTarget)\n            igDeltas[igKey] = (igDeltas[igKey] || 0) + transfer\n            return\n        }\n\n        var targets = this.blocksMatching(state, this.toScope, this.toTarget)\n        for (var t = 0; t < targets.length; t++) {\n            var id = targets[t].id\n            blockDeltas[id] = (blockDeltas[id] || 0) + transfer\n        }\n    }\n\n    accumulateSelfFeedback(state, q, blockDeltas, igDeltas, mult) {\n        if (this.toScope === 'ig') {\n            var igKey = this.igProsperityKey(this.toTarget)\n            var igVal = q[igKey]\n            if (igVal == null) { igVal = igProsperityDefault(this.toTarget) }\n            var igTransfer = this.coefficient * this.basisAmount(igVal) * mult\n            if (igTransfer !== 0) {\n                igDeltas[igKey] = (igDeltas[igKey] || 0) + igTransfer\n            }\n            return\n        }\n\n        var targets = this.blocksMatching(state, this.toScope, this.toTarget)\n        for (var t = 0; t < targets.length; t++) {\n            var block = targets[t]\n            var fromBlocks = this.blocksMatching(state, this.fromScope, this.fromTarget)\n            var matchesFrom = false\n            for (var f = 0; f < fromBlocks.length; f++) {\n                if (fromBlocks[f].id === block.id) {\n                    matchesFrom = true\n                    break\n                }\n            }\n            if (!matchesFrom) { continue }\n            var selfTransfer = this.coefficient * this.basisAmount(block.prosperity) * mult\n            if (selfTransfer !== 0) {\n                blockDeltas[block.id] = (blockDeltas[block.id] || 0) + selfTransfer\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfunction clampProsperity(value) {\n    var lo = Q.prosperityClampMin != null ? Q.prosperityClampMin : PROSPERITY_CLAMP_MIN\n    var hi = Q.prosperityClampMax != null ? Q.prosperityClampMax : PROSPERITY_CLAMP_MAX\n    return Math.max(lo, Math.min(hi, value))\n}\n\nfunction igProsperityDefault(igId) {\n    if (igId && PROSPERITY_IG_START[igId] != null) {\n        return PROSPERITY_IG_START[igId]\n    }\n    return PROSPERITY_IG_DISPLAY_BASE\n}\n\nfunction igIdFromProsperityKey(igKey) {\n    var slug = String(igKey || '').replace(/^prosperity_/, '').toLowerCase()\n    for (var name in PROSPERITY_IG_START) {\n        if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(PROSPERITY_IG_START, name)) {\n            continue\n        }\n        if (name.toLowerCase() === slug) { return name }\n    }\n    return null\n}\n\nfunction defaultProsperityForConnection(mod) {\n    if (!mod) { return PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE }\n    if (mod.fromScope === 'ig') {\n        return igProsperityDefault(mod.fromTarget)\n    }\n    if (mod.toScope === 'ig') {\n        return igProsperityDefault(mod.toTarget)\n    }\n    return PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE\n}\n\nfunction economyQualityExcess(q, qualityKey) {\n    var raw = Number(q[qualityKey])\n    if (isNaN(raw)) { raw = 1 }\n    return raw - 1\n}\n\n/** 2·sourcePop / (sourcePop + targetPop); IG sources use effective pop below. */\nfunction prosperityTransferMultiplier(sourcePop, targetPop) {\n    var a = Number(sourcePop)\n    var b = Number(targetPop)\n    if (isNaN(a) || isNaN(b) || a <= 0 || b <= 0) { return 0 }\n    return (2 * a) / (a + b)\n}\n\nfunction prosperityBlocksInDistrict(state, districtId) {\n    if (!state || !state.blocks) { return [] }\n    return state.blocks.filter(function(b) {\n        return b.district.id === districtId && b.population > 0\n    })\n}\n\nfunction prosperityDistrictTotalPop(state, districtId) {\n    var blocks = prosperityBlocksInDistrict(state, districtId)\n    var sum = 0\n    for (var i = 0; i < blocks.length; i++) {\n        sum += blocks[i].population\n    }\n    return sum\n}\n\nfunction prosperityIntraMeshCoeff(matrix, fromSid, toSid) {\n    if (!matrix || !fromSid || !toSid || fromSid === toSid) { return 0 }\n    var row = matrix[fromSid]\n    if (!row) { return 0 }\n    var c = row[toSid]\n    if (c == null || c === 0) { return 0 }\n    return Number(c)\n}\n\n\n/** Fixed footprint for corp/syndicate prosperity spill (not district pop). */\nvar PROSPERITY_IG_EFFECTIVE_POP = {\n    Soylent: 152,\n    Magrail: 148,\n    Brazos: 146,\n    Families: 44,\n    Edges: 42,\n    Sharks: 41,\n}\n\nvar PROSPERITY_DISTRICT_IDS = [\n    'Docks', 'Aurora', 'Vats', 'Railyard', 'Pitts', 'Limelight', 'Deeps',\n]\n\n/**\n * Within-district: every stratum block → every other stratum block in that district.\n * Sparse coeffs; missing pair = 0. Same default matrix in all districts unless\n * Q.prosperityIntraDistrictMesh[districtId] overrides.\n */\nvar PROSPERITY_INTRA_DISTRICT_DEFAULT = {\n    rich: {\n        first: 0.0005, second: 0.0015, coop: 0.0004, drone: 0, alien: 0,\n        deeper: 0, third_wave: 0,\n    },\n    first: {\n        rich: 0.0003, second: 0.002, coop: 0.001, drone: 0.0004, alien: 0,\n        deeper: 0, third_wave: 0,\n    },\n    second: {\n        rich: 0.0004, first: 0.002, coop: 0.0012, drone: 0.0005, alien: 0,\n        deeper: 0, third_wave: 0,\n    },\n    coop: {\n        rich: 0.0003, first: 0.001, second: 0.001, drone: 0.0006, alien: 0,\n        deeper: 0, third_wave: 0,\n    },\n    drone: {\n        rich: 0, first: 0.0003, second: 0.0004, coop: 0.0008, alien: 0,\n        deeper: 0, third_wave: 0,\n    },\n    alien: {\n        rich: 0, first: 0, second: 0, coop: 0, drone: 0, deeper: 0.0004,\n        third_wave: 0,\n    },\n    deeper: {\n        rich: 0, first: 0, second: 0, coop: 0, drone: 0, alien: 0.0004,\n        third_wave: 0,\n    },\n    third_wave: {\n        rich: 0, first: 0.0004, second: 0.0006, coop: 0.0004, drone: 0,\n        alien: 0, deeper: 0,\n    },\n}\n\n/**\n * IG prosperity → each stratum block in that IG's home district only.\n * Listed strata with 0 still wired ( no transfer).\n */\nvar PROSPERITY_IG_HOME_DISTRICT_LINKS = [\n    {\n        ig: 'Soylent',\n        district: 'Vats',\n        toStrata: {\n            rich: 0.001, first: 0.001, second: 0.0015, coop: 0.002,\n            drone: 0.009, alien: 0, deeper: 0.0005, third_wave: 0,\n        },\n    },\n    {\n        ig: 'Magrail',\n        district: 'Railyard',\n        toStrata: {\n            rich: 0.001, first: 0.0012, second: 0.001, coop: 0.0035,\n            drone: 0.008, alien: 0, deeper: 0.0005, third_wave: 0,\n        },\n    },\n    {\n        ig: 'Brazos',\n        district: 'Limelight',\n        toStrata: {\n            rich: 0.0012, first: 0.004, second: 0.0015, coop: 0.002,\n            drone: 0.008, alien: 0, deeper: 0.0005, third_wave: 0,\n        },\n    },\n    {\n        ig: 'Families',\n        district: 'Pitts',\n        toStrata: {\n            rich: 0, first: 0.002, second: 0.004, coop: 0.002,\n            drone: 0, alien: 0, deeper: 0.0008, third_wave: 0,\n        },\n    },\n    {\n        ig: 'Edges',\n        district: 'Railyard',\n        toStrata: {\n            rich: 0.0008, first: 0.0025, second: 0.003, coop: 0.0015,\n            drone: 0.0025, alien: 0, deeper: 0.0005, third_wave: 0,\n        },\n    },\n    {\n        ig: 'Sharks',\n        district: 'Deeps',\n        toStrata: {\n            rich: 0.0006, first: 0.001, second: 0.001, coop: 0.0008,\n            drone: 0, alien: 0.003, deeper: 0.005, third_wave: 0,\n        },\n    },\n]\n\n/** All strata wired in Docks trade spill (per-stratum multiplier × base coeff). */\nvar PROSPERITY_DOCKS_TRADE_STRATA = {\n    rich: 1.2, first: 1, second: 1, coop: 0.9, drone: 0.8,\n    alien: 0.7, deeper: 0.7, third_wave: 0.8,\n}\n\n/** trade_level excess → every block in Docks (basis: value − 1). */\nvar PROSPERITY_DOCKS_TRADE = {\n    district: 'Docks',\n    quality: 'trade_level',\n    coefficient: 0.01,\n    strata: PROSPERITY_DOCKS_TRADE_STRATA,\n}\n\n/** crime_level excess → listed strata in Pitts only. */\nvar PROSPERITY_PITTS_CRIME = {\n    district: 'Pitts',\n    quality: 'crime_level',\n    coefficient: -0.012,\n    strata: {\n        first: 1, second: 1, third_wave: 1, coop: 1, deeper: 1, alien: 1,\n    },\n}\n\nfunction applyDistrictIntraProsperityMesh(state, blockDeltas) {\n    var districts = Q.prosperityDistrictIds || PROSPERITY_DISTRICT_IDS\n    var defaultMesh = Q.prosperityIntraDistrictMeshDefault || PROSPERITY_INTRA_DISTRICT_DEFAULT\n    var perDistrict = Q.prosperityIntraDistrictMesh || null\n\n    for (var d = 0; d < districts.length; d++) {\n        var districtId = districts[d]\n        var matrix = (perDistrict && perDistrict[districtId])\n            ? perDistrict[districtId]\n            : defaultMesh\n        var blocks = prosperityBlocksInDistrict(state, districtId)\n        if (blocks.length < 2) { continue }\n\n        for (var si = 0; si < blocks.length; si++) {\n            var source = blocks[si]\n            var fromSid = source.demographic.id\n            var signal = source.prosperity ?? PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE\n            for (var ti = 0; ti < blocks.length; ti++) {\n                var target = blocks[ti]\n                if (source.id === target.id) { continue }\n                var coeff = prosperityIntraMeshCoeff(\n                    matrix,\n                    fromSid,\n                    target.demographic.id\n                )\n                if (coeff === 0) { continue }\n                var weight = prosperityTransferMultiplier(\n                    source.population,\n                    target.population\n                )\n                var transfer = coeff * signal * weight\n                if (transfer === 0) { continue }\n                blockDeltas[target.id] = (blockDeltas[target.id] || 0) + transfer\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfunction applyIgHomeDistrictProsperityLinks(state, q, blockDeltas) {\n    var links = Q.prosperityIgHomeDistrictLinks || PROSPERITY_IG_HOME_DISTRICT_LINKS\n    for (var li = 0; li < links.length; li++) {\n        var row = links[li]\n        var igKey = 'prosperity_' + String(row.ig).toLowerCase()\n        var igVal = q[igKey]\n        if (igVal == null) { igVal = igProsperityDefault(row.ig) }\n        var signal = Number(igVal)\n        if (isNaN(signal)) { signal = igProsperityDefault(row.ig) }\n        var sourcePop = PROSPERITY_IG_EFFECTIVE_POP[row.ig]\n        if (sourcePop == null) { sourcePop = 20 }\n        var blocks = prosperityBlocksInDistrict(state, row.district)\n        var toStrata = row.toStrata || {}\n\n        for (var bi = 0; bi < blocks.length; bi++) {\n            var block = blocks[bi]\n            var sid = block.demographic.id\n            if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(toStrata, sid)) {\n                continue\n            }\n            var coeff = Number(toStrata[sid])\n            if (isNaN(coeff) || coeff === 0) { continue }\n            var weight = prosperityTransferMultiplier(sourcePop, block.population)\n            var transfer = coeff * signal * weight\n            if (transfer === 0) { continue }\n            blockDeltas[block.id] = (blockDeltas[block.id] || 0) + transfer\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfunction applyDocksTradeProsperityLinks(state, q, blockDeltas) {\n    var spec = Q.prosperityDocksTrade || PROSPERITY_DOCKS_TRADE\n    var excess = economyQualityExcess(q, spec.quality)\n    if (excess === 0) { return }\n    var sourcePop = prosperityDistrictTotalPop(state, spec.district)\n    if (sourcePop <= 0) { return }\n    var blocks = prosperityBlocksInDistrict(state, spec.district)\n    var strataCoeffs = spec.strata || {}\n\n    for (var bi = 0; bi < blocks.length; bi++) {\n        var block = blocks[bi]\n        var sid = block.demographic.id\n        if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(strataCoeffs, sid)) {\n            continue\n        }\n        var strataMult = Number(strataCoeffs[sid])\n        if (isNaN(strataMult) || strataMult === 0) { continue }\n        var coeff = Number(spec.coefficient) * strataMult\n        if (isNaN(coeff) || coeff === 0) { continue }\n        var weight = prosperityTransferMultiplier(sourcePop, block.population)\n        var transfer = coeff * excess * weight\n        if (transfer === 0) { continue }\n        blockDeltas[block.id] = (blockDeltas[block.id] || 0) + transfer\n    }\n}\n\nfunction applyPittsCrimeProsperityLinks(state, q, blockDeltas) {\n    var spec = Q.prosperityPittsCrime || PROSPERITY_PITTS_CRIME\n    var excess = economyQualityExcess(q, spec.quality)\n    if (excess === 0) { return }\n    var sourcePop = prosperityDistrictTotalPop(state, spec.district)\n    if (sourcePop <= 0) { return }\n    var blocks = prosperityBlocksInDistrict(state, spec.district)\n    var strataCoeffs = spec.strata || {}\n    var baseCoeff = Number(spec.coefficient)\n    if (isNaN(baseCoeff)) { baseCoeff = 0 }\n\n    for (var bi = 0; bi < blocks.length; bi++) {\n        var block = blocks[bi]\n        var sid = block.demographic.id\n        if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(strataCoeffs, sid)) { continue }\n        var strataMult = Number(strataCoeffs[sid])\n        if (isNaN(strataMult) || strataMult === 0) { continue }\n        var coeff = baseCoeff * strataMult\n        var weight = prosperityTransferMultiplier(sourcePop, block.population)\n        var transfer = coeff * excess * weight\n        if (transfer === 0) { continue }\n        blockDeltas[block.id] = (blockDeltas[block.id] || 0) + transfer\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * One-shot citywide prosperity grants per stratum via Q.<stratum>_bump (e.g. coop_bump).\n * Adds bump to every voter block in that class, clamps, syncs Q, then sets the key to 0.\n * Cards:  on-arrival: coop_bump = 0.05\n * Same month: call Q.applyStratumProsperityBumps() in on-arrival after setting bump.\n * Otherwise applied at the start of monthly_tick_phase1 (before connection bleed).\n */\nfunction applyStratumProsperityBumps() {\n    var state = Q.electionV2\n    if (!state || !state.blocks) { return false }\n\n    var strata = Q.stratum_labels || [\n        'rich', 'first', 'second', 'coop', 'drone', 'alien', 'deeper', 'third_wave',\n    ]\n    var changed = false\n\n    for (var s = 0; s < strata.length; s++) {\n        var sid = strata[s]\n        var key = sid + '_bump'\n        var raw = Q[key]\n        if (raw == null || raw === 0) {\n            Q[key] = 0\n            continue\n        }\n        var bump = Number(raw)\n        Q[key] = 0\n        if (isNaN(bump) || bump === 0) { continue }\n\n        for (var i = 0; i < state.blocks.length; i++) {\n            var block = state.blocks[i]\n            if (block.demographic.id !== sid) { continue }\n            block.prosperity = clampProsperity(\n                (block.prosperity ?? PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE) + bump\n            )\n        }\n        changed = true\n    }\n\n    if (changed && typeof Q.qified_block_prosperity === 'function') {\n        Q.qified_block_prosperity()\n    }\n    return changed\n}\n\nfunction applyProsperityConnections() {\n    var state = Q.electionV2\n    if (!state || !state.blocks || !Q.prosperityConnectionCatalog) { return }\n\n    initEconomyProsperity()\n\n    var blockDeltas = {}\n    var igDeltas = {}\n    var catalog = Q.prosperityConnectionCatalog\n\n    for (var i = 0; i < catalog.length; i++) {\n        catalog[i].accumulate(state, Q, blockDeltas, igDeltas)\n    }\n\n    applyDistrictIntraProsperityMesh(state, blockDeltas)\n    applyIgHomeDistrictProsperityLinks(state, Q, blockDeltas)\n    applyDocksTradeProsperityLinks(state, Q, blockDeltas)\n    applyPittsCrimeProsperityLinks(state, Q, blockDeltas)\n\n    for (var b = 0; b < state.blocks.length; b++) {\n        var block = state.blocks[b]\n        var delta = blockDeltas[block.id]\n        if (delta) {\n            block.prosperity = clampProsperity(\n                (block.prosperity ?? PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE) + delta\n            )\n        }\n    }\n\n    for (var igKey in igDeltas) {\n        if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(igDeltas, igKey)) { continue }\n        var igVal = Q[igKey]\n        if (igVal == null) {\n            igVal = igProsperityDefault(igIdFromProsperityKey(igKey))\n        }\n        Q[igKey] = clampProsperity(igVal + igDeltas[igKey])\n    }\n\n    if (typeof Q.qified_block_prosperity === 'function') {\n        Q.qified_block_prosperity()\n    }\n}\n\nQ.ProsperityConnectionModifier = ProsperityConnectionModifier\n\n// Legacy rows (decay, card stacks). District mesh + home IG + Docks/Pitts: constants above.\nQ.prosperityConnectionCatalog = [\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_rich', 'stratum', 'rich', 'stratum', 'rich', -0.05, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_first', 'stratum', 'first', 'stratum', 'first', -0.05, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_second', 'stratum', 'second', 'stratum', 'second', -0.105, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_coop', 'stratum', 'coop', 'stratum', 'coop', -0.25, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_drone', 'stratum', 'drone', 'stratum', 'drone', -0.02, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_alien', 'stratum', 'alien', 'stratum', 'alien', -0.02, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_deeper', 'stratum', 'deeper', 'stratum', 'deeper', -0.02, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_third_wave', 'stratum', 'third_wave', 'stratum', 'third_wave', -0.05, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_soylent', 'ig', 'Soylent', 'ig', 'Soylent', -0.30, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_magrail', 'ig', 'Magrail', 'ig', 'Magrail', -0.30, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_brazos', 'ig', 'Brazos', 'ig', 'Brazos', -0.30, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_families', 'ig', 'Families', 'ig', 'Families', -0.02, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_edges', 'ig', 'Edges', 'ig', 'Edges', -0.02, { self_feedback: true }),\n    new ProsperityConnectionModifier('decay_sharks', 'ig', 'Sharks', 'ig', 'Sharks', -0.02, { self_feedback: true }),\n]\n\nQ.prosperityIntraDistrictMeshDefault = PROSPERITY_INTRA_DISTRICT_DEFAULT\nQ.prosperityIgHomeDistrictLinks = PROSPERITY_IG_HOME_DISTRICT_LINKS\nQ.prosperityDocksTrade = PROSPERITY_DOCKS_TRADE\nQ.prosperityPittsCrime = Police jurisdiction — reprisal on the corp that loses district security.\nCABLE_NEG_REPR_VATS_SOYLENT = 2          // @take_vats_police\nCABLE_NEG_REPR_RAILYARD_MAGRAIL = 2      // @take_railyard_police\nCABLE_NEG_REPR_DOCKS_SOYLENT = 1           // @take_docks_police (each belligerent)\nCABLE_NEG_REPR_DOCKS_MAGRAIL = 1\nCABLE_NEG_REPR_LIMELIGHT_BRAZOS = 3      // @take_limelight_police (needs Vats/Railyard/Docks)\n\n// Rival schadenfreude — reprisal lowered on corps that enjoy a rival's setback (always < gross raise).\nCABLE_NEG_RELIEF_VATS_MAGRAIL = 1        // Magrail likes Soylent losing Vats security\nCABLE_NEG_RELIEF_RAILYARD_SOYLENT = 1    // Soylent likes Magrail losing Railyard security\nCABLE_NEG_RELIEF_DOCKS_BRAZOS = 1        // Brazos likes both asymmetric)\nCABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_10X_MAGRAIL = 1\nCABLE_NEG_REPR_PAY_10X_BRAZOS = 2\n\n// Security tax — reprisal on taxed corps (requires payroll demand first).\nCABLE_NEG_REPR_TAX_HALF_BELL_SOYLENT = Q[corp + '_reprisal'] = (Number(Q[corp + '_reprisal']) || 0) + delta\n}\nQ.cableNegReprisalAddEach = function(delta) {\n    Q.cableNegReprisalAdd('soylent', delta)\n    Q.cableNegReprisalAdd('magrail', delta)\n    Q.cableNegReprisalAdd('brazos', delta)\n}\nQ.cableNegReprisalSub = function(corp, delta) {\n    Q[corp + '_reprisal'] = Math.max(0, (Number(Q[corp + '_reprisal']) || 0) - delta)\n}\nQ.cableNegEffectiveRelief = function(downs, grossUp) {\n    var i, grossDown = 0, out = []\n    downs = downs || []\n    if (grossUp < 2) { return out }\n    for (i = 0; i < downs.length; i++) {\n        if (downs[i].n > 0) { out.push({ corp: downs[i].corp, n: downs[i].n }) }\n    }\n    for (i = 0; i < out.length; i++) { grossDown += out[i].n }\n    if (grossDown >= grossUp) {\n        var budget = grossUp - 1\n        for (i = 0; i < out.length; i++) {\n            if (budget <= 0) { out[i].n = 0 }\n            else if (out[i].n > budget) { out[i].n = budget; budget = 0 }\n            else { budget -= out[i].n }\n        }\n    }\n    return out\n}\nQ.cableNegApplyWithRivalRelief = function(ups, downs) {\n    var i, grossUp = 0\n    ups = ups || []\n    for (i = 0; i < ups.length; i++) { grossUp += ups[i].n }\n    downs = Q.cableNegEffectiveRelief(downs, grossUp)\n    for (i = 0; i < ups.length; i++) { Q.cableNegReprisalAdd(ups[i].corp, ups[i].n) }\n    for (i = 0; i < downs.length; i++) {\n        if (downs[i].n > 0) { Q.cableNegReprisalSub(downs[i].corp, downs[i].n) }\n    }\n}\nQ.cableNegUndoWithRivalRelief = function(ups, downs) {\n    var i, grossUp = 0\n    ups = ups || []\n    for (i = 0; i < ups.length; i++) { grossUp += ups[i].n }\n    downs = Q.cableNegEffectiveRelief(downs, grossUp)\n    for (i = 0; i < ups.length; i++) { Q.cableNegReprisalSub(ups[i].corp, ups[i].n) }\n    for (i = 0; i < downs.length; i++) {\n        if (downs[i].n > 0) { Q.cableNegReprisalAdd(downs[i].corp, downs[i].n) }\n    }\n}\nQ.cableNegApplyVatsPolice = function() {\n    Q.cableNegApplyWithRivalRelief(\n        [{ corp: 'soylent', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_REPR_VATS_SOYLENT }],\n        [{ corp: 'magrail', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_VATS_MAGRAIL }]\n    )\n}\nQ.cableNegClearVatsPolice = function() {\n    Q.cableNegUndoWithRivalRelief(\n        [{ corp: 'soylent', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_REPR_VATS_SOYLENT }],\n        [{ corp: 'magrail', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_VATS_MAGRAIL }]\n    )\n}\nQ.cableNegApplyRailyardPolice = function() {\n    Q.cableNegApplyWithRivalRelief(\n        [{ corp: 'magrail', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_REPR_RAILYARD_MAGRAIL }],\n        [{ corp: 'soylent', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_RAILYARD_SOYLENT }]\n    )\n}\nQ.cableNegClearRailyardPolice = function() {\n    Q.cableNegUndoWithRivalRelief(\n        [{ corp: 'magrail', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_REPR_RAILYARD_MAGRAIL }],\n        [{ corp: 'soylent', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_RAILYARD_SOYLENT }]\n    )\n}\nQ.cableNegApplyDocksPolice = function() {\n    Q.cableNegApplyWithRivalRelief(\n        [\n            { corp: 'soylent', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_REPR_DOCKS_SOYLENT },\n            { corp: 'magrail', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_REPR_DOCKS_MAGRAIL }\n        ],\n        [{ corp: 'brazos', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_DOCKS_BRAZOS }]\n    )\n}\nQ.cableNegClearDocksPolice = function() {\n [{ corp: 'brazos', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_DOCKS_BRAZOS }]\n    )\n}\nQ.cableNegApplyLimelightPolice = function() {\n    Q.cableNegApplyWithRivalRelief(\n        [{ corp: 'brazos', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_REPR_LIMELIGHT_BRAZOS }],\n        [\n            { corp: 'soylent', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_LIMELIGHT_SOYLENT },\n            { corp: 'magrail', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_LIMELIGHT_MAGRAIL }\n        ]\n    )\n}\nQ.cableNegClearLimelightPolice = function() {\n    Q.cableNegUndoWithRivalRelief(\n        [{ corp: 'brazos', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_REPR_LIMELIGHT_BRAZOS }],\n        [\n            { corp: 'soylent', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_LIMELIGHT_SOYLENT },\n            { corp: 'magrail', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_LIMELIGHT_MAGRAIL }\n        ]\n    )\n}\nQ.cableNegApplyTaxHalfBelligerents = function() {\n    Q.cableNegApplyWithRivalRelief(\n        [\n            { corp: 'soylent', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_REPR_TAX_HALF_BELL_SOYLENT },\n            { corp: 'magrail', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_REPR_TAX_HALF_BELL_MAGRAIL }\n        ],\n        [{ corp: 'brazos', n: Q.CABLE_NEG_RELIEF_TAX_BELL_BRAZOS }]\n    )\n}\nQ.cableNegClearTaxHalfBelligerents = function() {\n
