No existing styles were found. I'll add a `syncMainHandActionDescription()` function in `organize_phase_tick` to sync the action display above the main hand.

The function will be called from `syncActionEconomyDisplay`. It sets `Q.handDescription` to two lines matching the politics tab. Since `organize_phase_start` precedes the main phase, the organizing unlock is already active when the player reaches main. Default text or hiding the description for dev paths or saves without the unlock still needs a decision.

When `organizing_unlock` is not yet 1, `handDescription` will be cleared so the default "Hand - click a card to play." text appears instead. Once unlocked, the function reads `action_reserve`, `month_actions_remaining`, `month_actions_used`, and `month_actions_limit` to build the two-line description.

The function builds a two-line string showing the action reserve and monthly usage. It updates both `Q.handDescription` and the `.hand-description` element. CSS will be added to `game.css` for that element. Static content in `main.scene.dry` is unnecessary.

The action stats will be appended below the default hand text rather than replacing it entirely. This keeps the existing "click a card to play" instruction visible while placing the action display above the hand.

A separate `organizing-actions-bar` div placed before the hand would be cleaner than appending text to `handDescription`. The `window.displayHand` function in `game.js` is being reviewed as another insertion point.

Wrapping `window.displayHand` in `game.js` was abandoned because it would recurse. A static HTML block in the main scene content would appear at the top above the decks, not above the hand itself.

}\n\n    isActive(q) {\n        try {\n            return !!this.activeIf(q)\n        } catch (e) {\n            return false\n        }\n    }\n\n    basisAmount(value) {\n        var v = }\n\n    blocksMatching(state, scope, target) {\n        if (!state || !state.blocks) { return [] }\n        if (scope === 'block') {\n            return state.blocks.filter(function(b) { return b.id pop\n            weighted += pop * (b.prosperity ?? t < targets.length; t++) {\n            var block = targets[t]\n            var fromBlocks = this.blocksMatching(state, this.fromScope, this.fromTarget)\n            var matchesFrom = false\n            for (var f = 0; ## [2026-06-07T16:40:19Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Organizing actions now show above the hand on main, using the same numbers as the Politics tab.

### How it works

Dendrynexus renders `Q.handDescription` as the paragraph directly above the hand cards. `syncMainHandActionDescription()` in `organize_phase_tick.scene.dry` sets that text whenever action stats sync (spend, month advance, landing on main):

```
Action reserve: 2/4
Actions available this month: 1 (1 of 3 used)

Hand — click a card to play.
```

### Changes

- **`organize_phase_tick.scene.dry`** — `syncMainHandActionDescription()` hooked into `syncActionEconomyDisplay()`; also updates the live `.hand-description` element when the hand is redrawn without a full page refresh
- **`main.scene.dry`** — `on-display` syncs stats right before the hand renders
- **`game.css`** — `white-space: pre-line` on `.hand-description` so the two-line action block displays cleanly

Politics tab display is unchanged. The banner only appears once `organizing_unlock = 1`.

## [2026-06-07T16:47:03Z] assistant_thought (afterAgentThought)

Planning a centralized `Q.applyActionSurgeIfNewPhase()` function to handle the action surge condition.

Identified three call sites for the surge check: `beginActionEconomyMonth`, `cable_break_negotiations` at phase 2, and any future phase transitions. The month-start flow clears the prior surge flag, applies the normal grant, then triggers the surge if it is the first month of a new phase.

Phase changes occur mid-month via events rather than at month ticks. A phase transition triggers the surge immediately. The following month advance clears the surge and restores normal limits. For example, a phase change in June activates the surge, while the next month’s advance resets it.

Mid-month surge activation adds two bonus actions to the reserve without capping it. The monthly spend limit is removed for the remainder of that month, allowing any actions already spent under normal limits to be replaced. The month-start sequence will record the prior action count before applying the surge.

The month-start sequence now explicitly checks whether the phase has advanced since the last surge grant before triggering the surge check. Because phases currently change mid-month, the surge should not fire during a standard month-start advance.

The surge flag and granted-through phase will initialize to zero in the scene dry state. The surge check itself will serve as a bug-recovery fallback if a phase change occurs without triggering the standard flow. Card choose logic remains compatible because it still checks remaining actions.

Updating the action economy display to reflect the surge state. When active, the UI will show "unlimited" instead of a capped usage count. A new `syncActionEconomyDisplay` helper will read the surge flag and monthly limit to drive the correct labels.

The `syncActionEconomyDisplay` helper clamps the reserve to its maximum when the surge is inactive. During a surge, it sets the remaining actions equal to the full reserve and bypasses the monthly limit entirely. Otherwise it computes remaining slots from the limit minus actions already used, capped by the reserve amount.

The `beginActionEconomyMonth` implementation now records the prior month's action count, clears the surge flag, resets the monthly action tally, and grants the standard reserve increase. It then invokes the surge check if the helper exists.

`applyActionSurgeIfNewPhase` is now fully implemented. It validates the current phase, skips activation if the surge was already granted for this phase, marks the phase as granted, sets the surge flag, adds the bonus actions to the reserve, and removes the monthly limit. The function returns true when it actually triggers the surge.

Verified the reserve math across surge scenarios. Starting phase 1 gives the reserve a +3 bump. Mid-month surge can push the reserve above 4, but the next month-start advance clamps it back to the maximum before granting the normal +1.

The hand banner will display the surge phase, current reserve, and uncapped spend count. The politics tab will use conditional prose to show the surge state. The helper belongs in setup_functions under ONGRANIZE_API. Cable negotiations will invoke it after the phase advances to 2. Phase starts already trigger the surge through beginActionEconomyMonth.

i < blocks.length; i++) {\n        sum += blocks[i].population\n    }\n    return sum\n}\n\nfunction prosperityIntraMeshCoeff(matrix, fromSid, toSid) {\n    if (!matrix || !fromSid || !toSid || fromSid === toSid) { return 0 }\n    var row = matrix[fromSid]\n    if (!row) { return 0 }\n    var c = row[toSid]\n    if (c == null || c === 0) { return 0 }\n    return Number(c)\n}\n\n\n/** Fixed footprint for corp/syndicate prosperity spill (not district pop). */\nvar PROSPERITY_IG_EFFECTIVE_POP = {\n    Soylent: 152,\n    Magrail: 148,\n    Brazos: 146,\n    Families: 44,\n    Edges: 42,\n    Sharks: 41,\n}\n\n/** Cable neg Docks DMZ — monthly IG prosperity while ceasefire lines favor one megacorp. */\nvar CABLE_DOCKS_DMZ_PROSP_GAIN = 0.06\nvar CABLE_DOCKS_DMZ_PROSP_RIVAL = -0.06\nvar CABLE_DOCKS_DMZ_PROSP_BRAZOS = -0.015\nvar CABLE_DOCKS_DMZ_PROSP_BELLIGERENT = -0.06\n\nvar PROSPERITY_DISTRICT_IDS = [\n    'Docks', 'Aurora', 'Vats', 'Railyard', 'Pitts', 'Limelight', 'Deeps',\n]\n\n/**\n * Within-district: every stratum block → every other stratum block in that district.\n * Sparse coeffs; ## [2026-06-07T16:47:18Z] assistant_thought (afterAgentThought)

A bug was found in `beginActionEconomyMonth` for the phase 1 surge.

`applyActionSurgeIfNewPhase` runs every month in `beginActionEconomyMonth`. This causes incorrect surges when the phase exceeds the granted count at month start.

The mid-month boundary bug is unlikely in practice. Future phase changes must also trigger `applyActionSurgeIfNewPhase()` when `Q.phase` is set directly.
```json
{
  "duration_ms": 2061
}
```

## [2026-06-07T16:47:30Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Implemented the **action surge** for the opening month of each phase.

### Rules
- **When:** First time each phase number is entered (`phase > action_surge_granted_through_phase`)
  - Phase 1: January 2300 via `organize_phase_start` → `beginActionEconomyMonth()`
  - Phase 2: When the cable ceasefire sets `phase = 2` (mid-month OK)
- **Bonus:** +2 to reserve (can go above the normal cap of 4)
- **Spend:** No monthly cap — you can spend the whole reserve that month
- **Duration:** Clears at the next `beginActionEconomyMonth()` (Advance); excess reserve above 4 is clamped back to 4 on that tick

### Example flow
| Month | Event | Reserve | Spend cap |
|-------|--------|---------|-----------|
| Jan 2300 | Phase 1 surge | 3 (1 monthly + 2 bonus) | Uncapped |
| Feb | Normal | 1 | 2/month |
| Jun 2301 | Phase 2 surge (cable deal) | +2 on current reserve | Uncapped rest of June |
| Jul | Normal | Clamped to 4 max | 2/month |

### Files touched
- `organize_phase_tick.scene.dry` — `applyActionSurgeIfNewPhase()`, surge-aware sync/display
- `cable_break_negotiations.scene.dry` — triggers surge when phase advances to 2
- `root.scene.dry` — init `action_surge_active`, `action_surge_granted_through_phase`
- `status.scene.dry` — Politics tab surge messaging
- `setup_functions.scene.dry` — bootstrap API list

Any future `Q.phase = N` should also call `Q.applyActionSurgeIfNewPhase()` so mid-month phase changes get the surge immediately.

t < targets.length; t++) {\n            var block = targets[t]\n            var fromBlocks = this.blocksMatching(state, this.fromScope, this.fromTarget)\n            var matchesFrom = false\n            for (var f = 0; ## [2026-06-07T16:52:16Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Two fixes:

### 1. Uncapped view stuck after month end
After a surge month, `month_actions_limit` stayed at **999** even when `action_surge_active` was cleared. `syncActionEconomyDisplay()` now treats any limit ≥ 999 as stale and restores the normal **2/3** cap from `actions_used_last_month`.

### 2. No surge at game start
`applyActionSurgeIfNewPhase()` now only runs for **phase 2+**. January 2300 (phase 1) gets the usual monthly grant (+1 reserve, 2–3/month cap) with no surge. The **first** surge is when cable negotiations set `phase = 2`.

| When | Surge? |
|------|--------|
| Jan 2300 (phase 1) | No — normal economy |
| Jun 2301 ceasefire (phase 2) | Yes — +2 reserve, uncapped spend |
| Phase 3+ opening month | Yes — same rules |

PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE = 6\n/** Corp/syndicate Q.prosperity_* at new game (root @start). */\nconst PROSPERITY_IG_START = {\n    Soylent: 10,\n    Magrail: 10,\n    Brazos: 10,\n    Families: 8,\n    Edges: 8,\n    Sharks: 8,\n}\n/** Display scale for stock / syndicate indices (prosperity 10 → baseline ticker). */\nconst PROSPERITY_IG_DISPLAY_BASE = 10\nconst PROSPERITY_CLAMP_MIN = 0\nconst prosperity as the source (stratum self-decay)\n * quality scope: fromTarget is a Q quality (e.g. trade_level); signal uses (value − 1) when basis is excess\n */\nclass ProsperityConnectionModifier {\n    constructor(rowId, fromScope, fromTarget, toScope, toTarget, coefficient, opts) {\n        if (rowId && typeof rowId === 'object') {\n            opts = rowId\n            rowId = opts.id\n            fromScope = opts.fromScope\n            fromTarget = opts.fromTarget\n            toScope = opts.toScope\n            toTarget = opts.toTarget\n            coefficient = opts.coefficient\n        } else if (typeof opts !== 'object' || opts === null) {\n            opts = {}\n        }\n        this.id = rowId\n        this.fromScope = fromScope\n        this.fromTarget = fromTarget || ''\n        this.toScope = toScope\n        this.toTarget = toTarget || ''\n        this.coefficient = coefficient || 0\n        this.basis = opts.basis || 'level'\n        this.self_feedback = !!(opts.self_feedback || opts.local)\n        this.stackId = opts.stackId || null\n        this.activeIf = opts.activeIf || function() { return true }\n    }\n\n    stacksFromQ(q) {\n        if (!this.stackId) { return 1 }\n        if (!q || q[this.stackId] == null) { return 0 }\n        var n = Number(q[this.stackId])\n        if (isNaN(n) || n <= 0) { return 0 }\n        return n\n    }\n\n    isActive(q) {\n        try {\n            return !!this.activeIf(q)\n        } catch (e) {\n            return false\n        }\n    }\n\n    basisAmount(value) {\n        var v = }\n\n    blocksMatching(state, scope, target) {\n        if (!state || !state.blocks) { return [] }\n        if (scope === 'block') {\n            return state.blocks.filter(function(b) { return b.id === target })\n        }\n        if (scope === 'stratum') {\n            return state.blocks.filter(function(b) { return b.demographic.id === target })\n        }\n        if (scope === 'district') {\n            return state.blocks.filter(function(b) { return b.district.id === target })\n        }\n        return []\n    }\n\n    weightedBlockProsperity(blocks) {\n        var popSum = 0\n        var weighted = 0\n        for (var i = 0; i < blocks.length; i++) {\n            var b = blocks[i]\n            var pop = b.population\n            if (pop <= 0) { continue }\n            popSum += pop\n            weighted += pop * (b.prosperity ?? PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE)\n        }\n        return popSum > 0 ? weighted / popSum : PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE\n    }\n\n    readBroadcastSource(state, q) {\n        if (this.fromScope === 'quality') {\n            var raw = Number(q[this.fromTarget])\n            if (isNaN(raw)) { raw = 1 }\n            return this.basisAmount(raw)\n        }\n        if (this.fromScope === 'ig') {\n            var key = this.igProsperityKey(this.fromTarget)\n            var igVal = q[key]\n            if (igVal == null) { igVal = igProsperityDefault(this.fromTarget) }\n            return this.basisAmount(igVal)\n        }\n        var blocks = this.blocksMatching(state, this.fromScope, this.fromTarget)\n        return this.basisAmount(this.weightedBlockProsperity(blocks))\n    }\n\n    accumulate(state, q, blockDeltas, igDeltas) {\n        if (!this.isActive(q)) { return }\n        var mult = this.stacksFromQ(q)\n        if (mult <= 0) { return }\n\n        if (this.self_feedback) {\n            this.accumulateSelfFeedback(state, q, blockDeltas, igDeltas, mult)\n            return\n        }\n\n        var sourceSignal = this.readBroadcastSource(state, q)\n        var transfer = this.coefficient * sourceSignal * mult\n        if (transfer === 0) { return }\n\n        if (this.toScope === 'ig') {\n            var igKey = this.igProsperityKey(this.toTarget)\n            igDeltas[igKey] = (igDeltas[igKey] || 0) + transfer\n            return\n        }\n\n        var targets = this.blocksMatching(state, this.toScope, this.toTarget)\n        for (var t = 0; t < targets.length; t++) {\n            var id = targets[t].id\n            blockDeltas[id] = (blockDeltas[id] || 0) + transfer\n        }\n    }\n\n    accumulateSelfFeedback(state, q, blockDeltas, igDeltas, mult) {\n        if (this.toScope === 'ig') {\n            var igKey = this.igProsperityKey(this.toTarget)\n            var igVal = q[igKey]\n            if (igVal == null) { igVal = igProsperityDefault(this.toTarget) }\n            var igTransfer = this.coefficient * this.basisAmount(igVal) * mult\n            if (igTransfer !== 0) {\n                igDeltas[igKey] = (igDeltas[igKey] || 0) + igTransfer\n            }\n            return\n        }\n\n        var targets = this.blocksMatching(state, this.toScope, this.toTarget)\n        for (var t = 0; Q.prosperityClampMin : PROSPERITY_CLAMP_MIN\n    var hi = Q.prosperityClampMax != null ? Q.prosperityClampMax : PROSPERITY_CLAMP_MAX\n    return Math.max(lo, Math.min(hi, value))\n}\n\nfunction igProsperityDefault(igId) {\n    if (igId && PROSPERITY_IG_START[igId] != null) {\n        return PROSPERITY_IG_START[igId]\n    }\n    return PROSPERITY_IG_DISPLAY_BASE\n}\n\nfunction igIdFromProsperityKey(igKey) {\n    var slug = String(igKey || '').replace(/^prosperity_/, '').toLowerCase()\n    for (var name in PROSPERITY_IG_START) {\n        if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(PROSPERITY_IG_START, name)) {\n            continue\n        }\n        if (name.toLowerCase() === slug) { return name }\n    }\n    return null\n}\n\nfunction defaultProsperityForConnection(mod) {\n    if (!mod) { return PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE }\n    if (mod.fromScope === 'ig') {\n        return igProsperityDefault(mod.fromTarget)\n    }\n    if (mod.toScope === 'ig') {\n        return igProsperityDefault(mod.toTarget)\n    }\n    return PROSPERITY_BLOCK_BASELINE\n}\n\nfunction economyQualityExcess(q, qualityKey) {\n    var raw = Number(q[qualityKey])\n    if (isNaN(raw)) { raw = 1 }\n    return raw - 1\n}\n\n/** 2·sourcePop / (sourcePop + targetPop); i < blocks.length; i++) {\n        sum += blocks[i].population\n    }\n    return sum\n}\n\nfunction prosperityIntraMeshCoeff(matrix, fromSid, toSid) {\n    if (!matrix || !fromSid || !toSid || fromSid === toSid) { return 0 }\n    var row = matrix[fromSid]\n    if (!row) { return 0 }\n    var c = row[toSid]\n    if (c == null || c === 0) { return 0 }\n    return Number(c)\n}\n\n\n/** Fixed footprint for corp/syndicate prosperity spill (not district pop). */\nvar PROSPERITY_IG_EFFECTIVE_POP = {\n    Soylent: 152,\n    Magrail: 148,\n    Brazos: 146,\n    Families: 44,\n    Edges: 42,\n    Sharks: 41,\n}\n\n/** Cable neg Docks DMZ — monthly IG prosperity while ceasefire lines favor one megacorp. */\nvar CABLE_DOCKS_DMZ_PROSP_GAIN = 0.06\nvar CABLE_DOCKS_DMZ_PROSP_RIVAL = -0.06\nvar CABLE_DOCKS_DMZ_PROSP_BRAZOS = -0.015\nvar CABLE_DOCKS_DMZ_PROSP_BELLIGERENT = -0.06\n\nvar PROSPERITY_DISTRICT_IDS = [\n    'Docks', 'Aurora', 'Vats', 'Railyard', 'Pitts', 'Limelight', 'Deeps',\n]\n\n/**\n * Within-district: every stratum block → every other stratum block in that district.\n * Sparse coeffs; ## [2026-06-07T16:58:32Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Here’s what was causing the blank flashes — they’re **silent setup/routing scenes** with no prose, not broken content.

### On startup (before `organize_phase_start`)

Two culprits, often the same flash:

1. **`organize_phase_tick`** — Bootstrap loads runtime APIs here (`max-visits: 1`, `new-page: false`, no body text). It was **missing `go-to: jumpScene`**, unlike every other runtime scene, so the engine could **stop on this blank page** instead of returning to `setup_functions`.

2. **`root.2300_main_continue`** — After bootstrap, `setup_functions` jumped here, which only contained `go-to: organize_phase_start` and no content. The “2300” intro prose in `root.scene.dry` sits **after** that `go-to`, so it never displayed.

You may also briefly see **`setup_functions`** and the other runtime scenes (`election_runtime`, etc.) — same pattern: no prose, immediate redirect.

### After advancing a month

**`post_event.events_choice`** — `advance.advance_month` was going **directly** to this empty subscene, **skipping** `post_event` itself. That meant:
- No month header (`February 2300`, etc.)
- **`post_event`’s `on-arrival` tick didn’t run** (projections, events check, routing to `main`)
- A blank page with only the event deck (or nothing if no events)

Same blank hop as going to `post_event.events_choice` without visiting the parent.

### Fixes applied

| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `organize_phase_tick` → `go-to: jumpScene` | Bootstrap completes instead of sticking on blank setup |
| Bootstrap jump → `organize_phase_start` directly | Drops the empty `root.2300_main_continue` hop |
| `advance.advance_month` → `go-to: post_event` | Runs the full month-end tick and routes to events or `main` |

Note: the “It is a dark time for humanity…” block in `root.scene.dry` is still orphaned (placed after `@2300_main_continue`’s `go-to`). Say if you want that woven into `organize_phase_start` or shown as its own intro scene.

## [2026-06-07T17:03:47Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Your memory matches the old Weimar-style pattern. Here’s what changed.

### How it used to work

The “dark time” block lives on `root.2300_main_continue` in `root.scene.dry`:

```154:161:source/scenes/root.scene.dry
@2300_main_continue
go-to: organize_phase_start

= 2300 

It is a dark time for humanity.  Earth is mired in endless national conflicts while the off planet colonies are torn by violence between lawless corporations.

As the corporations of the interplanetary waystation Mikasa become too distracted fighting each other, real power has started to fall into the hands of the city government for the first time in decades.  Now our task is to somehow maintain this newfound autonomy while beating back corruption.  Perhaps Mikasa might one day control the corporations instead of the other way around.
```

That mirrors the old `@1928_main` → `go-to: main` flow: show the year heading and intro prose, then enter the hand scene.

For that to appear **above the decks on main**, `main` must **not** clear the page. Originally `main.scene.dry` had no `new-page:` (there was even a `# TODO: should this really be a new page?` comment). With `new-page: false`, Dendry **appends** main’s hand UI below whatever `2300_main_continue` just rendered — so the intro stayed visible above the cards.

### Why it stopped

**1. `new-page: true` on `main` (May 25, commit `8dde925`)**

Adding `new-page: true` to `main` makes every arrival call `$content.empty()` before drawing the hand. The intro from `2300_main_continue` is wiped as soon as main loads, even if bootstrap still visits that scene first.

**2. Bootstrap destination changed (May 26, commit `303e172`)**

`2300_main_continue` was changed from `go-to: main` to `go-to: organize_phase_start`. First landing after bootstrap became the political-situation event, not main — so the intro–main pairing broke even if it had still been visible.

**3. Bootstrap skip (recent blank-scene fix)**

`setup_functions` now jumps straight to `organize_phase_start`, so `root.2300_main_continue` never runs and the intro never displays at all.

### Summary

| When | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| Originally | `2300_main_continue` shows intro → `main` (no `new-page`) → intro stays above hand |
| May 25 `8dde925` | `main` gets `new-page: true` → intro cleared on first main visit |
| May 26 `303e172` | Bootstrap goes to `organize_phase_start` instead of `main` |
| Recent | Bootstrap skips `2300_main_continue` entirely |

The prose is still in source and still compiles onto `root.2300_main_continue`; it’s the routing and `new-page: true` on `main` that prevent it from showing above the hand.

If you want it back, sensible options are: put the intro in `main.scene.dry` behind a one-shot flag (`main_intro_seen`), restore the `2300_main_continue` hop and drop `new-page` on first main visit only, or show it on `organize_phase_start` before the political text. I can implement whichever you prefer.

## [2026-06-07T17:20:25Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Two separate things were going on: a **calendar mismatch** for September Convention, and a couple of **event-queue bugs** that could cause real skips earlier in the year.

## Why September Convention doesn’t fire in November

The event is gated to **October 2300**, not November:

```6:6:source/scenes/events/september_convention.scene.dry
view-if: month = 10 and year = 2300
```

The roadmap also lists it under **Oct 2300**. It appears when you **Advance from September → October** (when `month` becomes 10). If you’re already in **November** (`month = 11`), the condition fails and the event is gone forever — it’s `max-visits: 1`.

The “November” in the event text is a **character title** (March Corporation spokesperson), not the calendar month.

## What *should* happen in November 2300

November is **Railyard district election month** (`DISTRICT_ELECTION_MONTH.Railyard = 11`). After Advance, `post_event` runs `runScheduledElections()`, which should set `elections_this_month = 1` and surface **`scheduled_elections`**, not September Convention.

## Fixes applied (for real skips)

1. **`has_event` detection** in `post_event.scene.dry` — now counts any choosable choice that isn’t “Continue back to main”, instead of comparing `choices[0].title` to the string `"Continue..."` (titles are display objects, not plain strings).

2. **Removed `tags: event` from `organize_phase_start`** — the opening “dark time” intro was in the `#event` pool. It’s scripted bootstrap content, not a monthly event, and could interfere with the event queue.

## If you already passed October

On an existing save where October was skipped (e.g. from the earlier Advance → `post_event.events_choice` bug that bypassed the tick/`has_event` check), September Convention won’t come back — one-shot events don’t retroactively fire.

**To verify:** start a new game, Advance through the months, and watch for September Convention when the calendar hits **October 2300**, and Council Elections in **November 2300**.

If November elections are also missing on a fresh run through that month, say so and we can trace `runScheduledElections` / `elections_this_month` on that path specifically.

## [2026-06-07T17:22:27Z] assistant_thought (afterAgentThought)

I'm examining the two-stage post_event flow to understand why events are still being skipped.

The skip likely stems from the silent root post_event immediately jumping to the events_choice subscene. I'll inspect how __changeScene handles subscene transitions and review the old has_event logic.

The old `has_event` check compares a display object title against a string literal. Because titles are objects, the condition always evaluates to true whenever choices exist. This means `has_event` was incorrectly set to 1 even when the only choice was "Continue..." with no actual events.

Real events are missing from _compileChoices. Possible causes include incorrect month filtering, exhausted max-visits, or the compilation running during post_event arrival with stale scene state.

The silent root post_event may be skipping the events_choice subscene entirely by jumping straight to main. A wrong rootSceneId could also miscount the Continue option. If events exist but all have canChoose=false, the skip is legitimate. September conventions lack choose-if restrictions, so this seems unlikely.

The compiled go-to target might be wrong because the silent parent cannot resolve the subscene ID. Alternatively, the jump to events_choice could succeed while the subscene itself fails to render the #event choices.

Reverting to a single-scene post_event is the cleanest path forward. The root scene should keep new-page: true and host the month heading again. The @events_choice split can be removed or kept but forced to run. The has_event check should be fixed so it only counts choices that are both selectable and not the root scene itself.

## [2026-06-07T17:23:56Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Yes — a partial rollback was the right call, but the fix is simpler than restoring the old `has_event` logic.

## What was wrong

The two-stage `post_event` (silent tick → `go-to` based on `has_event`) was the problem:

1. **`has_event` could false-negative** — our stricter check skipped to `main` when the old code would still have opened the event page.
2. **Errors in `on-arrival` are swallowed** by the engine (`console.log` only). If anything in the tick or `_compileChoices` threw, `has_event` stayed `0` and you went straight to `main`.
3. **`new-page: false` on the tick stage** added another layer where the month-end screen could flash blank before routing.

The old `choices[0].title != "Continue..."` check looked broken (titles are display objects, not strings), but it almost always set `has_event = 1`, so it rarely skipped real events — it mostly failed the other way (empty event pages).

## What I changed

`post_event` is back to a **single scene**:

- `new-page: true`
- Month tick runs in `on-arrival`
- Month heading + `#event` choices on the same scene
- **No `has_event` gate, no `@events_choice` subscene**

When there are events, they show. When there aren't, Dendry adds **Continue...** back to main automatically — that's the built-in behavior this flow should rely on.

## Calendar reminder

| Month | What should appear |
|-------|-------------------|
| **October 2300** | September Convention (`month = 10`) |
| **November 2300** | Railyard council elections (`scheduled_elections`) |
| **February 2300** | Vats district elections |

September Convention will **not** fire in November — that's by design in the scene file.

## To verify

Rebuild is done (`npm run make-html`). Start a **new game**, Advance to **October 2300**, and you should see the convention. If an old save already passed October without visiting it, that one-shot event won't come back (`max-visits: 1`).

If events still skip on a fresh run through October, tell me what month the UI shows when you Advance and we can trace from there.

Need to hide the Continue button on empty months without breaking the event display. The previous has_event approach broke the display.

The previous approach likely failed due to a fragile has_event check, new-page: false, or _compileChoices timing issues during on-arrival.

The engine always renders the Continue button when no events are present. To hide it safely, either route to main when empty while keeping #event on the same scene, or use a reliable has_event check on that same scene.

The previous failure came from splitting to a `@events_choice` subscene and compiling choices during on-arrival. A safer single-scene approach would compile choices on `post_event` itself during on-arrival, then route to `main` if only Continue appears. However, `go-to` executes after on-arrival for all scenes, so this may not work cleanly.

A single conditional `go-to: main if has_event = 0` solves the routing cleanly. When no events exist, the engine jumps straight to main and skips the Continue page entirely. When events exist, no go-to matches, so the scene simply displays its choices. This avoids splitting into a subscene or relying on fragile choice compilation during on-arrival.

The subscene split was likely the bug. Compiling choices for `post_event.events_choice` during on-arrival on the parent scene probably behaves differently than compiling for the scene that actually holds the options. The fix is to compile choices directly on `post_event` itself, count its choosable non-root choices to set `has_event`, and keep `new-page: true` on that same scene.

The exact implementation compiles choices for `post_event` directly rather than a subscene. It sets `Q.has_event` to 1 only when a compiled choice is both choosable and not the root scene ID, ensuring the Continue button alone does not trigger an event jump.

Yes — the trick is to **skip to main without splitting the scene**.

What broke events before wasn’t the `has_event` idea itself; it was compiling choices on a **separate `@events_choice` subscene** while `#event` lived elsewhere. The check and the display were out of sync.

The fix keeps the working layout (tick + `#event` on the same `post_event` scene) and adds a single conditional exit:

```18:28:source/scenes/post_event.scene.dry
Q.has_event = 0;
var choices = this._compileChoices(this.game.scenes['post_event']);
if (choices) {
    var rootId = this.state.rootSceneId;
    for (var ci = 0; ci < choices.length; ci++) {
        var ch = choices[ci];
        if (ch.canChoose && ch.id !== rootId) {
            Q.has_event = 1;
            break;
        }
    }
}
```

```41:41:source/scenes/post_event.scene.dry
go-to: main if has_event = 0
```

Behavior:

- **No events** — only “Continue back to main” would appear → `has_event = 0` → jump straight to `main` (no Continue screen).
- **Events exist** — at least one choosable non-main choice → `has_event = 1` → no `go-to` fires → the scene shows the event list as before.

The check runs **after** `runScheduledElections()` so election months still count. Build passes — try advancing through a quiet month (should land on main) and October/November (should show events).
